title: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation
snippet: Microsoft president Brad Smith calls for urgent AI regulation, saying milk and washing machines have more oversight than AI companies.
fullText:
Microsoft president Brad Smith is calling for urgent regulation of AI, and his argument is that consumer products like milk and washing machines have more oversight than the companies building artificial intelligence.

On a recent BBC podcast, Smith called AI both a “weapon and a tool” that is putting the world’s cybersecurity at risk and said the “moment has arrived” to institute global safety rules.

Smith also said the U.K., and not the U.S. or European Union, is best placed to lead on global safety rules. Britain’s AI Security Institute (AISI), launched in 2023, receives access to major models from U.S. frontier labs before they are deployed and has quickly become a leader in AI safety testing. 

That role has been under threat in recent weeks, with U.S. president Donald Trump warning against “globalist” organizations, which he claims are interfering with American companies. Last month, he reportedly asked Anthropic and OpenAI to withhold new models from British testers, but AISI confirmed on Monday that it is able to access and test the latest models. 

Despite the president’s pushback, however, Smith argued the U.K. can regulate AI in ways that the U.S. cannot. 

“In Washington, D.C., people don’t look at the U.K. and they don’t look at London the way they look at Brussels,” he told the BBC. “That’s a strength.”

His comments come amid rallying cries from tech leaders, including Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and OpenAI’s Sam Altman, to slow the pace of AI development in the wake of several incidents where AI agents went rogue.

Last month, Trump hosted tech leaders of companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, AMD, SpaceX, Meta, and Google, at the White House to discuss AI safety. They signed a “morally binding” document in which they agreed to work with “independent auditors” to assess the safety and capabilities of their AI models. 

Smith says the document is a “good step,” but it stops short of the type of regulation that is necessary. The problem with voluntary self-regulation, he said, is that only the “good companies” will comply. 

“It’s the companies that are not as responsible that you need to worry about,” he said.

Smith outlined several AI safety rules he’d like to see put into place, like a legal obligation to alert an organization if its system was breached by rogue AI agents. He also appears to be in favor of AI labs getting the approval of outside evaluators before an AI product is released and spoke positively about kill switches to pause or slow down AI if humans lose control of it. 

“Let’s speak calmly, maybe even softly, but firmly, and start to bring people together,” Smith said. “I hope that’s the role we can play as a company. I hope that’s the role the U.K. can play as a country.”

by  Stevie Bonifield

Oct 13, 2026, 3:12 PM UTC

Illustration: Alex Castro / The Verge

Stevie Bonifield

 

is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Epic Games plans to use AI to generate code and art for an unannounced Disney game, which is now delayed from its original March release window, according to a report from Bloomberg. The project’s developers have been given an “AI-first” mandate directing them to use tools like Anthropic’s Claude more to finish the game.

According to Bloomberg, one of the game’s directors said in a message to staff, “No more hand-written code.” Staff were also told that all of the game’s art will be “generated with full AI workflows.” In a statement given to Bloomberg, Epic Games spokesperson Jake Jones said the company is “embracing AI-accelerated development.”

Epic Games and Disney did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The upcoming game is reportedly a shooter featuring characters from Marvel and Star Wars. It’s part of a multiyear collaboration between Epic and Disney, which also invested $1.5 billion in Epic in 2024. Epic already uses AI in Fortnite, which has previously featured Disney characters like an AI Darth Vader. But it sounds like Epic may be aiming to have AI do most of the heavy lifting on its new Disney game.

AI game development tools have been popping up from other large companies, like Meta and Google, so Epic isn’t alone here. Epic CEO Tim Sweeney has also pushed for Steam to drop its “made with AI” tag, arguing that “AI will be involved in nearly all future production.” Earlier this year, Epic laid off over 1,000 of its employees, following a “downturn” in engagement on Fortnite since 2025.

title: Apple unveils Apple Home Collection smart home accessories developed with LG and Schneider
snippet: Apple today confirmed that it is working with at least two third-party companies to develop a new lineup of smart home accessories, including cameras, thermostats, and a smart lock. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple today confirmed that it is working with at least two third-party companies to develop a new lineup of smart home accessories, including cameras, thermostats, and a smart lock. Here are the details.

’Clean, minimal aesthetic and premium materials’

In addition to announcing the new Apple TV 4K, the new HomePod mini, and the new $299 HomeView smart display today, Apple also unveiled Apple Home Collection, a lineup of smart home accessories developed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.

Apple says it collaborated with both companies to bring “the simplicity, reliability, and privacy of iPhone and Apple Home to a new suite of smart cameras, thermostats, and a door lock.”

Building on the thousands of Works with Apple Home and Matter accessories available today, Apple Home Collection offers customers a new array of recommended products to better understand what’s happening inside and outside their home, manage access, and keep the temperature just right throughout the day.

The Apple Home Collection lineup currently includes the following products, with prices starting at:

LG Floodlight Cam: $399.95

LG Indoor Cam Plug-in: $199.95

LG Outdoor Cam Plug-in: $299.95

LG Smart Deadbolt Lock: $349.95

LG Smart Thermostat: $199.95

LG Temperature Sensor: $39.95

LG Video Doorbell Wired: $249.95

Schneider Home Smart Thermostat: $199.95

Schneider Home Smart Thermostat Room Sensor: $39.95

You can find more details about color and regional availability here. Apple says availability for the lineup begins in December, with some accessories not arriving until early 2027.

The new Apple Home Collection can be set up with one tap on the iPhone. From there, the entire lineup can be managed through the Apple Home app, with no separate apps or accounts required.

All accessories support Thread, while the smart lock also supports Matter and Aliro, allowing its core access functions to work locally, even without an internet connection.

Apple says all data in the Home app is end-to-end encrypted, meaning neither Apple nor its partners, LG Electronics and Schneider Electric, can access it.

Here’s Apple on the home monitoring lineup:

LG’s lineup of four cameras gives users a private and intelligent way to monitor their homes when using a home hub like Apple HomeView, HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K. Every camera captures up to 2.5K resolution video and recognizes people, familiar faces, pets, vehicles, and packages, with video history securely stored in users’ supported iCloud+ plan, so there’s no separate camera subscription.

The cameras also support Apple Intelligence features, including automatic video summaries that describe what’s happening in recorded footage, and the ability to search recordings using natural language. Both features require an eligible iCloud+ subscription and compatible Apple devices.

As for home access, which is handled by LG’s Smart Deadbolt Lock, Apple confirms that it supports Ultra Wideband, which in practice means the door can automatically unlock when someone approaches with a compatible iPhone or Apple Watch configured with a home key, without needing to tap either device.

	

It also features an integrated PIN pad and a hidden backup key slot, and can detect when the door has been opened, closed, or tampered with, including alerting users if it remains open while locked.

When it comes to the Home Climate products, Apple explains that the new thermostats from LG and Schneider Electric can automatically adjust temperatures based on whether users are home, getting ready for bed, or away, without requiring manual scheduling. They can also use temperature and humidity readings from sensors placed in different rooms.

Schneider Electric’s Smart Thermostat on the left, LG’s Smart Thermostat on the right.

Finally, Apple says that starting this fall in the U.S., customers will be able to pay an additional fee to have their Apple Home Collection accessories professionally installed by ADT through Apple Retail.

Who said all privacy protections had to be digital nowadays? In my line of work, traveling can be common, and working from a coffee shop, train, or hotel lounge is something I do on the regular. So when I came across this nifty privacy app that knows to blur your screen the second you look away, I was enthralled.

The app is called ShyGlass, and it comes from developer Max Rovensky, who posted a 10-second demo on X last month that has since racked up over 230,000 views. The way it works is pretty simple. While wearing a pair of AirPods, if you turn your head to a certain degree, your MacBook screen blurs. When you turn your head back, the screen unblurs itself.

Behind the scenes, it’s using the motion sensors Apple uses for dynamic head tracking in Spatial Audio, the feature that keeps your music anchored when you look around. ShyGlass uses the same motion data but to detect presence. A user calibrates a center position from the menu bar, and anytime head positioning drifts past a set angle (15° by default, adjustable from 2° to 30°), a blur fades in over the display until it’s fully covered.

Now this is Security Bite after all, so I have a couple of thoughts on the permission the app needs: Screen Recording. ShyGlass does need to pull a snapshot of a user’s display to apply the blur effect, which kind of sounds a little ironic for a privacy tool. According to the developer, the snapshot stays in memory and is never saved or uploaded, and capture stops the moment the blur does.

I have no reason to doubt that. But it’s worth bring up the trade here. Screen Recording is one of the most powerful permissions on the Mac. An app with it can see everything you see, all the time, and macOS has no way of enforcing that it only looks when it says it does. So you’re basically taking the developer at his word.

Still, I find its functionality useful more often than not. Like turning to chat with the person next to you on a flight, or digging through your bag in a public space. Any time your head leaves the screen, there’s a window where someone else’s eyes can land on whatever you’re working on.

I hope to see Apple implement a macOS feature like this one day.

But if you want to check out ShyGlass, the developer has it priced at $4. It’s available on macOS 14 or later and requires AirPods 3 or later, any AirPods Pro, or AirPods Max.

title: Apple makes another push into the smart home market with HomeView
snippet: Apple is taking a big swing at the smart home market with its latest product that competes with Amazon Echo Show and Google Nest Hub.
fullText:
Apple is taking a big swing at the smart home market. The company on Tuesday unveiled its long-rumored smart home hub, dubbed HomeView, that can act as a central control point for smart home devices, be used for FaceTime calls, playing music, watching videos, displaying photo slideshows, and more. 

The new $299 device looks like a cuboid version of the HomePod, but with a display added to the front. The HomeView comes in two versions: one can sit on a countertop, and the other can be mounted on a wall. Measuring 7 inches wide, the hub features a single FaceTime camera on the front, and has microphones and speakers built into its base. 

Apple has preloaded the device with several of its apps, including Calendar, Messages, Photos, FaceTime, Notes, Reminders, Music, and Podcasts. That means users won’t need to reach for their iPhone if they want to check a calendar appointment, send a message, play some music, or look at photos.

Apple sees the device being particularly useful in places such as the kitchen. Someone cooking dinner, for example, could pull up a recipe, watch a video, check a calendar, or start a FaceTime call without resorting to their phone. 

Image Credits:Apple

It’ll also act as a smart home dashboard, allowing users to ask Siri to view camera feeds, adjust the thermostat, turn on lights, and lock doors. This comes as Apple announced its lineup of smart home accessories today, including a smart deadbolt lock, security cameras, and doorbell. Users will hear a chime from their HomeView when someone is at the door, for example. 

One of the more interesting aspects of the device is how it works with different members of a household.

The hub runs Apple’s updated Siri AI assistant and can recognize individual people in the house. Once it identifies someone, the screen can show information meant for that person, such as their messages, contacts, calendar appointments, notes, and preferred apps. The experience changes automatically when another family member walks up to the device.

The company says HomeView can recognize up to six people. 

HomeView puts Apple in a much more direct fight with Amazon and Google, both of which already have established smart display products: Amazon has its Echo Show line, while Google offers the Nest Hub.

Apple has had a mixed history in the smart home space, however, with products such as the HomePod struggling to reach the same level of popularity as competing devices. The new hub is an opportunity for Apple to change that by combining home controls with the company’s wider ecosystem.

The device has been rumored for quite some time, with reports pointing to delays caused in part by problems with Siri AI. Those issues have reportedly affected Apple’s broader smart home plans as well.

Image Credits:Apple

This may only be the first phase of Apple’s smart home plan. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has previously reported that Apple could eventually take the concept further with a more advanced version that features a robotic arm. Such a device could move its display and interact in a more physical way.

Preorders start today, and the device will be available to buy from November 13. It comes in four colors: silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray.

title: Gemini app rolling out Gemini 4 Argon to AI Pro and AI Ultra
snippet: Following the announcement at the end of September, Gemini 4 Argon is starting to roll out to the Gemini app, Google Antigravity, and more. more…
fullText:
Following the announcement at the end of September, Gemini 4 Argon is starting to roll out to the Gemini app, Google Antigravity, and more.

Gemini app 

In the Gemini app, Gemini 4 Argon is available for both Google AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers. Last month, initial availability was just for the Ultra ($99.99+) tier. 

Google says to expect “frontier reasoning and improved performance across complex workflows” in the app. Additionally:

“Argon answers questions more directly with less hedging, doesn’t repeat itself more than necessary, and skips clichés throughout the responses.” Additionally, it “follows style instructions more reliably than any of our previous Gemini models.”

“For longer tasks, it keeps you in the loop by sharing its progress more often and more effectively.”

Given the “major improvements” in coding performance, Google is letting users “switch between chatting and coding” within the Gemini app for macOS. Users will specifically have direct access to Antigravity’s agentic coding interface in the consumer client for building apps, web experiences, and more.

	

Meanwhile, there will be a new toggle in the main chat window that lets you switch from chat to tasks (previously Spark). As of today, AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers will see 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.8 Flash, 3.1 Pro, and 4 Argon in the model picker.

AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers can also access Gemini 4 Argon in AI Mode.

Google Antigravity + more

In the Antigravity desktop app and Antigravity CLI, the new model requires AI Ultra. Google today shared more examples of how it has been using Argon with its internal version of Antigravity across Chrome, Gemma, YouTube, and more:

“Argon helped the Chrome team separate core webpage handling from a ~6 million line legacy folder of browser features held within Chromium’s 40 million-line codebase. Piping multiple clean code changes at a time, Argon helped the team finish an architectural refactor across hundreds of files, completing months of work in weeks. For Chrome’s billions of global users, this will unlock the ability for live webpages to move fluidly between tabs, side panels, and floating windows without reloading, eliminating an entire category of browser crashes.”

“Using Argon, we achieved a 2.85x end-to-end inference speedup on an A100 via vLLM (accelerating throughput from ~37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second on Gemma 4 E2B) with 100% token parity and zero quality drop in just a few days, a process that would usually take months. Check out the upstream pull requests (optimizing everything from attention tuning to speculative decoding) to see the exact changes.”

“Argon in Antigravity helped the team cut the CPU footprint of YouTube’s comments frontend in half. By tracing production profile data, Argon identified that redundant emoji rendering alone accounted for nearly 45% of server overhead, leading to 12 targeted optimizations. The updates reduced server comment-load latency by 30 ms and dropped client end-to-end latency by 20 ms.”

AI Ultra is also required for Argon access in AI Studio and Android Studio (Canary).

Argon is available in the Gemini API at an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until November 30, 2026. Afterward, it will cost $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens.

On the science front, Google is offering 10,000 scientists the “highest usage tier in Google Antigravity free of charge for 6 months.” Applications are now open.

title: Amex introduces a framework to prevent AI agents from making unauthorized purchases
snippet: American Express is introducing a new framework designed to ensure AI agents only make purchases their users have authorized, potentially preventing costly mistakes and disputes as AI-powered shopping grows.
fullText:
Personal AI agents are increasingly making transactions on their users’ behalf, but given the nondeterministic nature of large language models, AI bots are prone to doing what they’re not supposed to. Which, in this case, raises the possibility of AI misfiring and making unauthorized transactions. 

To get ahead of this problem, American Express is introducing a new framework designed to capture and authenticate a customer’s purchase intent before an AI agent completes the transaction.

The idea is that there should be a way to ensure that the customer’s purchase instructions are carried throughout the transaction lifecycle, Amex says, from the purchase to everything that follows.

Dubbed the “Intent Intelligence Framework,” the company hopes it will become an industry standard for AI-powered transactions.

“These new transactions will have a consumer, a merchant, and an agent,” explained Amex’s VP of Agentic Partnerships and Strategy, Hannah Bozian, in an interview with TechCrunch. She said the company wanted to ensure that agentic transactions are still “seamless, trusted, and secure, the way our card members expect them to be.” 

This framework’s release follows the company’s April launch of Amex’s Agentic Commerce Experiences, or the ACE Developer Toolkit, which includes a handful of services that now include the intent framework.

Amex said it has not yet seen an increase in disputes because of agentic commerce, but it wanted to be proactive in building this technology as this type of commerce scales. In part, that’s because consumers have signaled they’re open to trying agentic commerce.

In a recent Amex Trendex report, 66% of surveyed U.S. consumers said they’re likely to use AI agents to research the best price for a product or service, and 61% said they’re likely to use it for a product or service recommendation over the next 12 months, the company told TechCrunch.

To start, Amex’s new intent framework begins with a Create Intent API, which will capture the customer’s purchase instructions along with other constraints they may have included in their request, like the merchant’s name, maximum budget, and other product preferences. How this intent is collected may vary depending on the AI model involved, but the plan is to make this framework flexible enough to support all agentic commerce models, Bozian said.

The customer then authenticates their identity and signs off on the intent captured by the agent. 

Then an Intent ID, a unique identifier representing the intent, is created, along with a Proof of Intent Token, which includes the customer’s high-level constraints. This token is used to obtain a secure digital payment credential that the agent will use at checkout instead of the customer’s actual credit card number. In doing so, Amex says, the purchase will remain secure while being aligned with what the customer authorized the agent to do.

This Intent ID and token can also be used in different parts of the transaction process, helping companies to manage areas like fraud prevention and dispute resolution, Amex said.

“Our approach differs from the implementations of others in that it pulls intent earlier into the transaction flow. And this is important because it helps mitigate some risk before the risk occurs,” said Bozian. She offered the example of a customer asking an agent to buy white Nike sneakers in a size 9, but the agent submits a request to purchase shoes from Adidas. In such a case, Amex could prevent the transaction from going through because the agent made a mistake.

Bozian also notes that while many agents today ask for customer consent before making a purchase, Amex foresees a future where agents may act much more autonomously in some cases. For instance, a consumer might allow their agent to re-order household staples, like paper towels or toilet paper — categories in which the only real constraint is the price and size, not merchant or brand. In these scenarios, it makes sense to have technology in the loop performing that extra check, to ensure the transactions match the customer’s intent.

Having a log of what was authorized by which agent and when could also help address fraud on behalf of the agent, she noted.

Amex is already in discussions with partners across the payments ecosystem for implementing ACE, which includes the agentic tokens that contain Amex’s payment credentials, as well as other parts of the developer kit.

The company said it plans to actively develop ACE further as the agentic commerce ecosystem evolves.

On October 13 at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026‘s Industry Stage, Amex VP of Agentic Partnerships and Strategy at American Express, Hannah Bozian, will discuss the company’s new “Intent Intelligence Framework” in more detail, and what it means for the world of agentic commerce.

title: I Tested the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s Batteries and Was Awestruck by One Change
snippet: Turns out the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have more to offer than just their fancy camera and new burgundy color. Both performed well in our battery tests.
fullText:
Battery life might be the iPhone 18 Pro’s sleeper feature.

When Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, the phones were instantly overshadowed by their new sibling, the iPhone Duo, which has a passport-size design with a tiny iPad-like folding screen. That doesn’t mean that Apple’s latest pro phones don’t have their own appeal.

On paper, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s marquee features are the new variable aperture and the addition of manual controls in the Camera app, aimed at the niche audience of professional photographers and creative types. But my testing found that the phone’s battery upgrades should appeal to everyone. That’s in part because the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have larger batteries than their 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max counterparts, as revealed in a teardown by the tech repair site iFixIt.

Beyond the increased battery capacity, the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have the power-efficient A20 Pro chip and run on iOS 27, which has several behind-the-scenes improvements to reduce power consumption. At a time when companies, including Apple, are raising phone prices – the 18 Pro starts at $1,199 and 18 Pro Max at $1,299 – it’s reassuring to see that the new Pro models are more than just a yearly iteration and improve on the 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max’s fast charging and long battery life.

How do they compare to the iPhone 17, iPhone Air and older iPhone models?

CNET tested the Apple phones’ four ways to find out: a battery stress test, a video streaming battery test, a wired charging test and a wireless charging test. These results, along with our lab data from previous years, show that the iPhone 18 Pro Max has the longest-lasting battery life of any phone Apple has ever made. The smaller iPhone 18 Pro is the fastest-charging iPhone. The performance of both phones in my testing and review is why each has earned a CNET Editors’ Choice Award.

		

			

Key takeaways

Lab testing across video streaming and battery stress tests shows that the 18 Pro Max delivers the longest overall battery life of any iPhone to date, driven by a larger battery capacity and the power-efficient A20 Pro chip and iOS 27.

The 18 Pro is Apple’s fastest-charging phone, reaching 53% battery in 15 minutes and 82% in 30 minutes.

Despite being a prior-generation model, the iPhone 16 Plus still holds the best score in the 45-minute multitasking battery stress test, edging out both the 17 Pro Max and 18 Pro Max by 1 percentage point.

The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have an incredible battery life

As part of my 45-minute endurance test, I played the game Arknights: Endfield to stress the phone’s battery.

CNET has two battery benchmark tests (video streaming and stress tests) to rate battery performance. We averaged the scores from both tests for each phone to determine the final ranking. If you’re looking for a phone with the longest battery life between charges, get an iPhone 18 Pro Max, which came out on top.

Because we’ve used these tests for years, we can compare new iPhones against older models. If you have an iPhone 15 or 16, upgrading to an iPhone 17 will get you a noticeably longer battery life out of the box. Keep in mind that display brightness, the strength of your carrier’s signal and how you use your phone all have a tremendous impact on the battery life you get from any phone. If you’re someone who is obsessively online, a phone with an incredible battery life might not be enough for you. Obviously, battery life isn’t the only consideration when shopping for a new phone, and normally, I’d recommend holding onto your phone for 3 to 4 years if possible.

In CNET’s 3-hour video battery test, where we streamed a video over Wi-Fi with the screen at full brightness, the iPhone 18 Pro had the highest remaining charge. What’s notable is how it did compared with the iPhone 17 Pro, which lost 8% more in the same test. That’s quite the improvement in just a single year. The $929 iPhone 17, $270 less than the 18 Pro, might be the most surprising result, placing fourth in the test. It proves you don’t need to buy a $1,300 phone to get great battery life. 

The iPhone 18 Pro Max landed second in the 3-hour streaming video test.

In CNET’s 45-minute battery stress test, during which I played games, streamed videos, scrolled social media and took a video call with the screen at half brightness, 2024’s iPhone 16 Plus still holds the best result. The 18 Pro Max and 17 Pro Max placed second, just a single percent behind the 16 Plus. The iPhone 17 lands in the third spot, again an impressive result that shows that the standard model will be more than enough for most people, even a year after it came out. The iPhone 18 Pro placed last in this test, but keep in mind that its result was better than many Android phones, such as the Pixel 11 Pro and Galaxy S26.

Looking at our results, the iPhone 17 Pro Max and 18 Pro Max are nearly identical in battery life, even though the new phone scored a percentage point higher in one test. So if you’re able to get a deal on the 17 Pro Max, Apple stopped selling it, save money, go for it.

The iPhone 18 Pro is the fastest charging iPhone

We run two 30-minute charging tests, one of which is for wired charging.

At some point, you’re going to need to recharge your iPhone’s battery and one discovery I had from testing was just how much Apple improved wired charging on both the new Pro models. We have two charging tests (wired and wireless) to rate recharging performance. As with our battery tests, we averaged the scores from the two tests to determine the final ranking. If you want the fastest-charging Apple phone, then buy an iPhone 18 Pro.

In our 30-minute wired charging test, starting with the battery at 0% and charging with the included cable, the iPhone 18 Pro added 82%, reaching 53% after 15 minutes. Compare that with the iPhone 17 Pro, which saw a 74% increase in the same test. That’s an 8% gain between model years and a wild improvement!

So why the big difference here? The iPhone 17 Pro supports 40-watt fast charging, whereas the iPhone 18 Pro supports 60-watt fast charging. Both require using or purchasing a wall plug that supports those speeds.

The 18 Pro Max added 77% in the same 30-minute test and hit 48% at the 15-minute mark. This is another 8% improvement from last year – the 17 Pro Max gained 69%.

Again, the notable performance came from the iPhone 17, which recharged its battery from empty to 69%, matching the 17 Pro Max.

The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max support 25-watt Qi2.2 wireless charging via MagSafe, like the 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max. In our 30-minute wireless charging test, the 17 Pro beat the new 18 Pro by just a single percent. The 18 Pro Max placed just after the iPhone Air in the same test. Keep in mind that the 18 Pro Max has the largest battery capacity of any iPhone we tested. Though the 17 Pro Max has a large battery, too, it came in third for this test.

The iPhone Duo and final thoughts

The iPhone Duo is Apple’s most innovative and expensive phone.Patrick Holland/CNET

Apple will release the iPhone Duo on Oct. 23. We are excited to test its battery and charging capabilities, but at this time, we’ve only had brief hands-on time with the foldable phone at Apple’s event last month.

While battery life and charging speeds are not the primary reasons to choose one iPhone over another, they are among the most important considerations. Out of Apple’s current lineup, the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max will give you the most battery life. But I think most people will be fine with the standard iPhone 17. Think of it as getting the most battery life for your dollar.

The iPhone Air is Apple’s slimmest phone (until the Duo goes on sale), but still has a good battery life despite its petite proportions. And while the iPhone 17E is Apple’s most affordable phone, it has a battery life that beats out most of the older iPhone models that we tested.

Lastly, if the poor battery health on your current iPhone is making you want to upgrade, it’s worth considering a battery replacement. It’ll cost you $50 to $130, depending on which model you have; even less if you replace it yourself. Doing so will add a couple more years to your phone’s longevity and save you hundreds of dollars.

When Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, the phones were instantly overshadowed by their new sibling, the iPhone Duo, which has a passport-size design with a tiny iPad-like folding screen. That doesn’t mean that Apple’s latest pro phones don’t have their own appeal.

title: Meta Launches Muse Wonder AI Models to Play Catch-Up With Rivals
snippet: The models build upon the Muse Spark AI model, launched earlier this year.
fullText:
Tech giant Meta debuted its new Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full premium AI models on Monday, continuing a push toward what CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently called the “AI frontier,” where the heavy hitters in the artificial intelligence space have dominated. 

The models build upon the Muse Spark AI model, launched earlier this year. Meta calls the new paid tiers its “most capable models to date,” reporting the models can perform personal and professional agentic tasks ranging from handling insurance claims to helping renters understand a lease agreement to building entire working apps.

Playing catch-up

Meta says its new models, the fruits of billions of dollars invested over the last year, leapfrog the competition. But it’s playing catch-up with Anthropic, OpenAI and Google in the AI race.

			

More from CNET

“Meta is making up for lost time with lots of new AI tools,” Katelyn Chedraoui, CNET’s expert reporter on artificial intelligence, told me. “But this new frontier model comes amid serious safety concerns in the AI industry. Safeguards will be essential to any new launch.”

Many researchers and experts are advocating for external evaluation and regulation of the technology, with some AI executives, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI’s Sam Altman, making high-profile calls to slow AI development. Meanwhile, Zuckerberg has been vocal in his belief that labs can and should self-police to stave off the worst effects of AI.

“I’m much closer to the belief that AI is a technology that can be engineered with normal guardrails and built responsibly than the anthropomorphic vision of AI, which is that it is just going to go do its own thing,” Zuckerberg told Financial Times in an interview this week.

Meta recently announced the Muse Charm AI hardware, which looks like a keychain or pendant.Meta/CNET

Muse Wonder and Wonder Full

Muse Wonder is the “state-of-the-art” premium-tier AI model from Meta. It is available first to coders who pay for access to the Meta Model API, via the Power Plan at $20 per month or the Maximum Plan at $100 per month. However, Meta’s announcement says it “will soon power experiences in Muse” with more flexible per-million-token pricing.

Meta says Muse Wonder builds on the core capabilities of its Muse Spark AI model with more advanced features, greater processing power and improved capability in law, finance and health applications. Meta gives the example of Muse parsing a leasing agreement or handling an insurance claim. (To be clear, do not rely on AI for healthcare or mental health.) Muse Wonder’s new “frontier coding performance” will also enable the agent to assist in building games and apps.

Muse Wonder introduces two new features: Active Memory and Active Focus.

The first, Active Memory, enables the model to remember and carry information across conversations. Storing potentially sensitive data immediately sets my privacy-conscious Spidey Sense on edge. That said, Meta says it has trained its Muse Wonder model to avoid sharing private information without permission and has hardened it against cyberattacks. The company even says that “developers and security teams can use models like Muse Wonder to find flaws in their own code and strengthen their systems,” which — I gotta be honest — sounds to me like the peak tech hubris. 

Meta’s CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, has been vocal in his belief that labs can and should self-police to stave off the worst effects of AI.James Martin/CNET

The second new feature, Active Focus, keeps the AI agent working when it runs into technical dead ends. With Active Focus, Muse Wonder is said to be capable of alternative approaches, recovering from errors and asking the user for clarification. That should let the model handle more complex tasks than Spark and encounter fewer roadblocks, which we’ve seen firsthand in our testing.

But boasting that your AI model can more effectively circumnavigate what may be blocks put in place (perhaps for a reason) sounds eerily familiar. Recently, Anthropic revoked access to its AI models, Mythos 5 and Fable 5, after the US government imposed sweeping restrictions on who could use them.

Muse Wonder Full is said to be an even more powerful version of the premium Wonder model with all of the same new features, but with a shift in focus toward businesses and power users. Basically, Wonder Full unlocks more flexible reasoning, a tweaked base model and access to more behind-the-scenes processing power, making it a better fit for unfamiliar tasks, engineering and professional workflows.

With no public API, Muse Wonder Full is available exclusively to developers who sign up for the paid Muse Code AI agent and is bundled into a monthly subscription priced from $50 to $200.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Antuan Goodwin
						

						

							Senior Writer, Electrified Cars						
					

											

								

											Antuan has nearly 20 years of expertise and experience testing hundreds of cars, including electric, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, hydrogen, and traditional combustion vehicles.

title: Free Gemini users now on ‘Auto’ models as app adds thinking levels
snippet: As announced last week, Google is rolling out a big change to the Gemini app experience for users on the free plan. Additionally, everyone is getting access to thinking or “effort” levels. more…
fullText:
As announced last week, Google is rolling out a big change to the Gemini app experience for users on the free plan. Additionally, everyone is getting access to thinking or “effort” levels.

Free users “without a plan” can no longer manually switch models. Officially, their only option in the picker is “Auto” with “Gemini 3 models.” Last week, Google’s support documentation referred to it as (3.5) Flash-Lite.

Google says: “Gemini will use auto model selection to send each prompt to the Gemini model that suits it best. Most prompts will go to Flash-Lite, our fastest model. Prompts that need deeper reasoning may go to Flash or Pro.”

Meanwhile:

	

If smart model selection is turned off, chats for users without an AI plan will use Flash-Lite for all responses.

Google is also rolling out new “effort levels” that replace the previous “Extended” option. These three choices align with “thinking levels” in Google AI Studio and Antigravity:

Low: Quick and efficient

Medium: Balanced depth

High: Extra thorough

We’re seeing the free change rolled out on the vast majority of our free accounts this evening (PT). Google appears to be rolling out this update quite quickly. 

The new effort levels will be available to all subscribers, and are also in the process of rolling out.

Meanwhile, Google AI Plus users will soon be limited to Flash-Lite and (3.8) Flash.

title: Apple HomePod Mini 2: Same Look but So Much Siri AI
snippet: The new Apple smart speaker, announced Tuesday, promises unique Siri interactions.
fullText:
Following Amazon’s new Echo Studio and Google’s Home Speaker release in the past year, it felt like Apple was left out of the upgrade cycle. Today’s “Welcome Home” event changed all that, revealing not only the luminous HomeView smart display, but also the next generation of the HomePod, called the HomePod Mini 2.

The small smart speaker, measuring about 4 inches across, will come equipped with the S10 chip, which Apple says analyzes music in real time to optimize it. Apple promises a future update will add an array of Siri AI features too, which is when this speaker should really get interesting.

The HomePod Mini 2 is available to preorder starting at $149 and comes in five new colors, including green and blue. It will arrive in stores on Oct. 30. As expected, Apple is sticking with the Mini line to help keep prices under control, although this model costs nearly $50 more than the previous HomePod Mini.

			

More from CNET

A Siri AI experience made for iPhones

The HomePod Mini 2 is available in five different colors.

Basic Siri voice commands are all available on the HomePod Mini 2, including the ability to ask questions, set reminders and control Apple Home devices, including the many new home security and smart home products also announced on the Tuesday event. So, what will the “AI” part add?

Apple is promising Siri AI will let HomePod Mini 2 owners tailor their interactions with the speaker to their own preferences and habits. By analyzing iPhone usage, Siri AI can use contextual data to answer commands more effectively. Apple gave the example of playing a song based on a past text message from a friend, even if you don’t really remember what the song is called. Another demo showed finding a recipe sent in an email and adding its ingredients to a shopping list. The latest Siri AI conversational features will also be available.

This sounds much like what Gemini for Home can do on the Google Home Speaker, but naturally more intertwined with Apple’s own apps. Also, full Gemini for Home features can cost up to $20 a month, but Apple didn’t provide much pricing information for these smart speaker AI features, so they could be significantly less or even free.

A few final tricks include the ability to hold a conversation out of the HomePod Mini 2 using the Home app on iPhone, as well as a feature that listens for fire alarms and alerts you when you’re not home. But how does the audio perform?

How does the new HomePod audio really sound?

The HomePod Mini 2 is equipped with a full-range driver and dual passive radiators, made for 360-degree sound. That sounds just like the design of the first-gen HomePod Mini, so it’s not immediately clear what Apple has done to enhance the audio beyond software adjustments.

You can also link up to four models together for surround sound. It also works with the new Apple TV 4K model, also announced at the event. However, music streamers take note: While the speaker supports Apple Music, TuneIn, iHeartRadio and Audacy, there’s no mention of support for popular apps such as Tidal and Spotify.

We look forward to testing the HomePod Mini 2 alongside other new smart speakers to see how the audio improvements really compare. The older HomePod Mini was showing its age compared to the Google Home Speaker the last time I tested them, especially in the lower register, so it will be interesting to see any changes.

							Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

With degrees in business management, literature and technical writing, Tyler takes every opportunity to play with the latest AI technology, push smart devices to their limits and occasionally throw cameras off his roof, all to find the best devices to trust in your life. He always checks with the renters (and pets) in his life to see what smart products can work for everyone, in every living situation. 
Living in beautiful Bend, Oregon, gives Tyler plenty of opportunities to test the latest tech in every kind of weather and temperature. But when not at work, he can be found hiking the trails, trying out a new food recipe for his loved ones, keeping up on his favorite reading or gaming with good friends.

title: Microsoft President Says AI Has Fewer Regulations Than Milk. So Now What?
snippet: Some tech executives say they want more regulation and safety guardrails, but critics are skeptical.
fullText:
The next time you pick up a carton of milk, consider this: It has likely passed through more safety inspections than the AI system writing your emails, screening your job application or negotiating with your bank. That, according to Microsoft President Brad Smith, is the problem.

In an interview with ITV last week, Smith said that AI is less regulated than milk and washing machines. He proposed that governments adopt established production safety practices and that AI companies build “kill switches,” a kind of emergency brake that would allow operators to shut down a system that begins behaving in an unsafe or unintended way. 

Smith’s comments come amid growing public concern that voluntary industry commitments to safety — a form of toothless self-regulation — are not enough to manage systems that can influence decisions, handle sensitive data and, in the wrong hands, enable cyberattacks. Recent cases of so-called “rogue AI agents” escaping their environments, such as the summer’s infamous Hugging Face hack and attempted breaches of Australian and US government websites, have drawn scrutiny to AI’s alleged “existential risk” and sparked calls for a pause.  

			

More from CNET

On Saturday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella echoed Smith’s sentiments in a lengthy X post, saying that the biggest companies lack a “mechanistic understanding” of the tools they deploy. Nadella also argued for slower development, incident reporting and independent review.

“We must build contained systems whose behavior we can observe, limits we can test and actions we can always contain,” Nadella wrote.

Microsoft’s statements come less than two weeks after top AI executives, including Nadella, met with President Donald Trump, who announced his proposal to rename AI as “super intelligence.“

Several Silicon Valley leaders — including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and xAI founder Elon Musk — signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, pledging to establish internal committees to oversee development and to work with independent auditors. (Though Microsoft doesn’t appear to have signed Trump’s voluntary accord, Nadella notably uses the term “super intelligence” in his recent X post.)

Smith’s and Nadella’s comments place Microsoft closer to Anthropic’s camp of “caution,” which calls for stronger AI oversight. Meanwhile, OpenAI’s Altman said that we should all just “accept some bad things happening” for the benefit of AI, whereas Zuckerberg and Huang continue to double down on their rejection of an industry-wide, coordinated slowdown in AI development. 

Wherever they stand on the regulation debate, AI leaders all stand to benefit in some way from engaging in the discussion on safety guardrails. For example, Microsoft recently released Microsoft Execution Containers, an enterprise security feature that protects devices by restricting the files and programs AI models can access and providing a built-in kill switch to instantly shut them down if needed.

A Microsoft representative declined to make any further comment.

The “rogue AI” narrative and Trump’s “super intelligence” rebrand serve as implicit marketing for the biggest AI companies — making them wealthier and more powerful.Cheng Xin/Getty Images

The ‘rogue AI’ narrative and Big Tech regulation

Despite increasingly public safety threats, it’s unlikely that the Trump administration will back regulation across the entire AI industry. The president has declared AI safety concerns a hoax, even as insiders report that more nuanced debates are unfolding behind closed doors. Last month, Trump posted on Truth Social that the only guardrail the AI industry needs is a “strong and smart president.”

In December 2025, Trump issued an executive order designed to prevent states from passing “cumbersome legislation” regulating AI model development, passing the buck to his own administration. The president continues to post online about maintaining a low-regulation environment for the biggest AI companies.

Many prominent AI critics argue that the entire regulatory framework is flawed from the start because it lets AI companies define the security threats and respond on their own terms. Distributed AI Research Institute founder Timnit Gebru has argued that the “rogue AI” narrative surrounding incidents like Hugging Face and access to government websites shifts attention away from basic corporate failures.

“This is not models going rogue,” Gebru told Democracy Now during an interview on Oct. 1. “This is gross incompetence and negligence by a particular company.” 

Gebru said that people need to understand that these fallible machines don’t act autonomously with their own agency. “We need to hold corporations liable for unleashing these kinds of error-prone models into the world,” she said.

According to Gebru, the focus on so-called runaway AI and the push for voluntary self-regulation are ways for the industry to avoid accountability under existing law. Rather than face liability for unsafe security practices occurring now, AI companies redirect the conversation to an unprecedented danger likely to occur in the future.

The real danger is regulatory capture, where AI companies shape the rules that are supposed to constrain them. In this way, the public is asked to trust the morality of the very companies that build and profit from AI.

title: Googlebook will improve support for Linux apps eventually, but it’s all about AI for now
snippet: Googlebook was always going to run into problems with app availability, but few expected the platform to regress its support for Linux apps from Chromebook’s fairly robust solution. In a blog post, Google reiterates that the “Linux Terminal Preview” on Googlebook isn’t for using Linux apps, but for building with AI. more…
fullText:
Googlebook was always going to run into problems with app availability, but few expected the platform to regress its support for Linux apps from Chromebook’s fairly robust solution. In a blog post, Google reiterates that the “Linux Terminal Preview” on Googlebook isn’t for using Linux apps, but for building with AI.

ChromeOS introduced support for Linux apps a few years ago, allowing users to install apps designed for Linux on their machines to expand what the laptops could do. Googlebook does not have this same support, with the Linux Terminal accessible and apps technically installable, but those apps now show up alongside Android and web apps, nor do they feature the same level of user-facing functionality.

In a blog post this week, Google reiterates that the priority around Linux support on Googlebook is, for now, focused on AI-aided app development. 

Today, getting the most out of AI workflows requires access to a terminal with a command line, even if someone doesn’t identify as a programmer or software developer. With Googlebook, we’re excited to help users express themselves and gain access to these tools. Googlebooks come with pre-installed tooling to get you going.

Google says that the Terminal is designed to be the “entry point” for AI agents so that tools like Google’s own Antigravity can use command-line tools within the Linux virtual machine. That setup also ensures your private files are isolated from the agent’s access (unless you grant access). 

	

The Linux Terminal implementation on Googlebook is “optimized for rapid prototyping, web development, scripting, and agentic workflows via CLI,” Google says, with a future focus on “building not only on Googlebook but also for your other devices” while also fine-tuning the experience for “heavier workloads.” 

Also directly mentioned is that Google is working on support for showing Linux GUI apps in the app launcher, which is the main downside to the current implementation. 

We can’t wait for the terminal and Linux VM to continue getting more capable over time, including Linux GUI app support with integration directly into the app launcher.

There’s no word on when this might arrive, but the focus right now is very much on AI and development. The rest of Google’s roadmap includes:

We are working hard to get you building not only on Googlebook but also for your other devices. In addition to the existing network passthrough and wireless ADB, USB passthrough and support for ADB over USB are coming, enabling local device debugging and more from our Linux VM and Antigravity. Learn more about Antigravity on Googlebook.

Our testers have been eager to run more complex tasks. To make this more seamless, we are adding dynamic memory and storage scaling for the VM.

We will be adding GPU/NPU hardware acceleration for heavier local workloads, allowing users to leverage the performance and power efficiency of dedicated hardware.

VM persistence and separation from the terminal window will better support long-running processes, when you want to take on more demanding agentic workloads.

title: Apple confirms HomePod mini 2 won’t have Siri AI at launch
snippet: Today Apple introduced HomePod mini 2 with Siri AI as a major tentpole feature. HomePod mini 2 ships on October 30, but checking the fine print on Apple’s website, it seems Siri AI won’t be available on launch day. more…
fullText:
Today Apple introduced HomePod mini 2 with Siri AI as a major tentpole feature. HomePod mini 2 ships on October 30, but checking the fine print on Apple’s website, it seems Siri AI won’t be available on launch day.

Siri AI coming to HomePod mini 2 in ‘a future software update’ per Apple

HomePod users have been waiting for Apple to reveal when Siri AI is coming to its home devices. And today it became official: Siri AI will be available soon on the new HomePod mini 2.

But unfortunately, if you buy HomePod mini 2 for launch day delivery on October 30, you’ll be left waiting a bit longer to access Siri AI.

From Apple’s website, in the ‘Meet Siri AI’ section for HomePod mini 2:

Siri on HomePod mini 2 puts a powerful, AI assistant right at the center of your home.1 Once set up with your iPhone or iPad, Siri draws on broad world knowledge and your personal context to help you find what you need and get more done every day.

Enjoy more natural conversations, richer answers, and effortless smart home control — while your privacy is protected at every step. Just ask to play your favorite music, check your schedule, or catch up on podcasts, completely hands-free.

1 Coming in a future software update. Usage limits may apply.

The footnote above says that Siri AI won’t be arriving until a future software update. This is further confirmed in Apple’s press release here near the bottom.

HomePod mini 2 arrives two weeks ahead of HomeView and the new Apple TV 4K, both of which ship November 13. Each of those products support Siri AI at launch, so here’s hoping that means HomePod mini 2 will gain support by mid-November too.

If that’s the case though, it’s certainly curious why Apple wouldn’t just launch all three products the same day with Siri AI.

When do you expect HomePod mini 2 to gain Siri AI support? Let us know in the comments.

title: Apple acqui-hires AI startup founded by former NotebookLM developers
snippet: The European Union’s Digital Markets Act transparency website lists Huxe as Apple’s newest acqui-hire, and at least the fourth AI-related deal disclosed this year. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
The European Union’s Digital Markets Act transparency website lists Huxe as Apple’s newest acqui-hire, and at least the fourth AI-related deal disclosed this year. Here are the details.

Apple’s latest AI deal involves former NotebookLM developers

In mid-2025, a team of three developers who worked on Google’s NotebookLM announced Huxe, their own personalized AI audio app that could generate daily briefings from a user’s email and calendar, create podcast-style conversations around specific topics, and provide continuously updated audio feeds for subjects such as news and sports.

NotebookLM, which was recently renamed as Gemini Notebook, is one of Google’s most popular AI products to date. It started as an experimental research and note-taking tool designed to answer questions and generate summaries based on a user’s own documents, and grew into a broader AI research assistant capable of creating podcast-style Audio Overviews, video summaries, study materials, and more.

In December 2024, as NotebookLM was exploding in popularity, project lead Raiza Martin left Google to found a new company, alongside two former NotebookLM colleagues: designer Jason Spielman and engineer Stephen Hughes.

They formally launched Huxe on an invite-only basis in June 2025, and opened it to everyone that September, alongside the announcement of a $4.6 million funding round.

Huxe continued developing its product until May 2026, when the company announced it was shutting down. The service ended on May 28. At the time, the company’s website said only that the team was “moving on to new things.”

Today, the European Union’s Digital Markets Act transparency database revealed that Apple has struck the following deal with Huxe, and informed the bloc last June:

09.06.2026   Huxe

Apple Inc. (“Apple”) will have the right to make employment offers to and hire certain employees of Huxe AI, Inc. (“Huxe”) and receive a non-exclusive license to Huxe’s intellectual property rights. Huxe provides a mobile application that creates personalized audio content. Apple designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells a variety of related services.

In other words, this is not an outright acquisition of the company, but rather the now-common acqui-hire structure in which a larger company brings over key employees and gains access to some of the startup’s technology without purchasing the business itself.

Although there are no details about what Apple plans to do with Huxe’s technology or which employees it intends to hire, the deal fits Apple’s pattern of recent AI acquisitions and acqui-hires of AI companies developing new ways for people and devices to interact through voice, vision, and other interfaces.

Acqui-hires have been criticized for potentially allowing large tech companies to sidestep traditional merger reviews.

Earlier this year, FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson said the agency was beginning to look closely at such arrangements, and in March, the FTC and Justice Department formally began considering changes to premerger reporting rules that could specifically address acqui-hires, reverse acqui-hires, and deals involving non-exclusive IP licenses.

There has been little public movement on that specific issue since then.

title: iPhone hits record Q3 shipment share as global smartphone market plunges 20%, per report
snippet: According to Counterpoint Research, Apple saw its share of global smartphone shipments cross 20% for the first time in a third quarter, despite an industry-wide decline. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
According to Counterpoint Research, Apple saw its share of global smartphone shipments cross 20% for the first time in a third quarter, despite an industry-wide decline. Here are the details.

’The second successive quarter to take the full brunt of the memory crisis’

In a report released today, Counterpoint Research says memory constraints and rising prices have pushed global smartphone shipments to their lowest third-quarter level in 14 years, with a 20% year-over-year decline. The report doesn’t say what that translates to in absolute numbers.

According to Counterpoint Research, Apple shipped 22% of all smartphones during Q3 2026, up from 18% in the year-ago period. That helped it narrow the gap with Samsung, which remained in first place with a 23% share.

The top five also included Xiaomi (10%), OPPO (9%), and vivo (8%), all of which saw their shipment shares decline compared to Q3 2025.

Here’s Counterpoint Research on Apple’s performance for the period:

Apple’s market share crossed 20% for the first time in any Q3, reaching 22%, despite a YoY decline in shipments. The volume decline was largely driven by the absence of a base iPhone 18, which resulted in a smaller launch-month channel fill than the full iPhone 17 lineup a year earlier. Apple also joined the industry wide shift toward price hikes, although the impact was limited to the final weeks of the quarter. However, the iPhone 18 Pro models saw a stronger launch than their predecessors, particularly in China and India, while sustained momentum from the iPhone 17 series helped offset a higher shipment decline.

Looking ahead, the report noted that things don’t look particularly encouraging for the remainder of the year, “with OEMs increasingly prioritizing profitability over shipment volumes amid elevated component costs and weaker affordability.”

Counterpoint added that price-sensitive segments will likely face further pressure from higher device prices and limited component availability, with a meaningful recovery in shipment volumes unlikely until costs come down and supply conditions improve.

title: Apple’s new smart home lineup includes a smart lock, thermostat, and video doorbells
snippet: The new devices work with HomeView, the company's new smart home hub which can be used to control accessories and interact with apps.
fullText:
Apple is getting serious about the smart home space. The company on Tuesday showed off its new Apple Home Collection, which includes a new smart deadbolt lock, video doorbell, thermostat, temperature sensor, and a range of security cameras.

The new devices are designed to work with HomeView, the company’s new smart home hub which can be used to control connected accessories and interact with Apple’s software.

This new range of smart home accessories could help Apple compete better with Amazon Ring and Google Nest, two established players in connected home security. The products will become available in December.

Apple says the devices were built in partnership with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric — an interesting move for the company, which has long sought to build and support every smart home accessory itself.

The smart lock, priced at $349.95, stands out for its support for ultra-wideband (UWB), a wireless technology that enables more precise proximity detection than traditional Bluetooth. This could allow the lock to recognize when an authorized user approaches and automatically unlock the door, reducing the need to pull out a phone or reach for a physical key.

The $249.95 wired video doorbell, meanwhile, will let homeowners see who’s outside, monitor visitors, and receive notifications when someone approaches their property. When someone rings it, a chime will sound through Apple devices like HomeView, HomePod, and HomePod mini. Users will also be notified on their iPhone or iPad.

As for the temperature sensor, it can provide insight into conditions in individual rooms, helping users identify temperature differences between areas and make adjustments.

For security, Apple is also introducing indoor and outdoor cameras, as well as a floodlight camera ($399.95) that combines exterior lighting with video monitoring. The camera lineup includes features such as live viewing, motion detection, intelligent alerts, and video storage.

title: Google’s SynthID AI content detector expands globally, will work on Apple’s models ‘soon’
snippet: Google’s AI-detector for images and videos, SynthID, is getting a full release today. It will work for more than just content developed with Google’s AI models and initial partners. more…
fullText:
Google’s AI-detector for images and videos, SynthID, is getting a full release today. It will work for more than just content developed with Google’s AI models and initial partners.

SynthID is a necessary tool as AI content has taken hold of heavy portions of the internet. Models have evolved so much that it’s nearly impossible to tell whether some videos or photos are even real, and it has you second-guessing whether real ones are generated. SynthID takes aim at that problem by introducing invisible watermarks at the generation stage, and when used on an image, it will detect those watermarks.

Of course, that only works if the image generation tool inserts its own footprint to begin with.

Google announced that SynthID is being upgraded from limited early access to a globally available tool in English, though it’s expected to expand further in the future. The tool has progressed some, but this is a bigger step for AI content detection. According to Google’s press release, the AI image detector launch comes with expanded compatibility.

	

The new SynthID will work with content generated on Google’s own Gemini, a given, as well as content from more partners. So far, the list includes OpenAI, Nvidia, Kakao, and now, Apple. That means any content generated with models from those companies will contain visually undetectable watermarks so users can later check whether the image is a human-made visual or something an algorithm cobbled together.

Google notes that images made with Apple Intelligence will carry a SynthID watermark “soon,” which implies it might be a little bit before users can reliably identify AI-generated content from Apple’s models. But the expansion means that more users in total will be able to do some due diligence on photos and videos posted online.

title: Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
snippet: The startup will sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million.
fullText:
Only five years into its journey, Character.AI, which lets users create AI characters and have conversations with them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, following a slew of lawsuits and struggles to scale its popular platform. In a court document, the company said it had assets and liabilities between $50 million and $100 million.

“Over the past year, Character.ai has taken meaningful steps to sustain and improve its business in the face of significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds. After a comprehensive review of the available alternatives, the board determined that this court-supervised sale process provides the Company with the best opportunity to maximize value for all stakeholders,” Character.AI CEO Colin Adams said in a statement.

The startup has also agreed to sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million, as well as a non-exclusive perpetual license for its technology.

The company said Disney will provide transition services via former Character.AI employees who joined the entertainment giant last month alongside its former CEO Karandeep Singh Anand.

Adams said the company would continue operating during the sale process, which is expected to close in late November or early December. However, he did note that there isn’t yet a bid for the company’s assets or a buyer.

“We hope that the sale process will yield an actionable proposal that will allow continued operations of the Character.ai platform. If such a bid is unavailable, however, the platform will be wound down,” Adams wrote.

Character.AI has had a tumultuous five years. Founded by former Google engineers Noam Shazeer, a co-author of the landmark Transformer paper, and Daniel De Freitas in late 2021, the startup initially focused on training foundation models and developing an AI chatbot platform that lets people create custom characters they could chat with.

By September 2022, the startup reached unicorn valuation with a $150 million fundraise on the back of high demand for its platform, with the company saying at the time that its users had exchanged more than 2 billion messages with its bots in five months, and active users were averaging more than two hours on the platform daily.

In May 2023, the Character.AI’s apps attracted more than 1.7 million installs in their first week after launch. But about a year later, in August 2024, Google struck a $2.7 billion deal to license the startup’s models, and both Shazeer and De Freitas returned to the search giant. At that time, the startup’s general counsel, Dominic Perella, stepped in as interim CEO, and the company moved away from training foundation models to focus on growth.

Character.AI’s traction didn’t slow, however, with its platform recording 20 million monthly active users by October of that year.

But things got difficult after the startup was sued following the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother says he became obsessed with a chatbot on its platform. Soon after, Texas launched an investigation to assess if the platform conformed to child privacy and safety laws. The company subsequently settled some of these lawsuits, added more safety features, and banned minors from its platform.

In June of last year, the company appointed Anand, a former Brex and Meta executive, as CEO, and expanded its products to add AI video generation, and social feeds. The company has since tried to introduce new ways to spur user engagement via interactive storytelling formats as well as microdramas.

But the fact that the company had to file for bankruptcy shows that such changes couldn’t move the needle on sustainability for the startup.

It also shows that consumer-facing AI products are really hard to scale and monetize. Character.AI was one of the top apps in terms of time spent, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower. But high engagement can be a double-edged sword; AI costs rise the more people use the app, which consequently also increases the pressure to monetize users.

Image Credits:Sensor Tower

Character.AI has raised over $193 million in funding across multiple rounds from investors including Lightspeed, SV Angel, Greycroft, and a16z, according to PitchBook.

title: Google releases officially refurbished Pixel 9 devices starting at $499 with an extra perk
snippet: After outing its Pixel 7 series in recent weeks, Google has just quietly released the Pixel 9 series to its Certified Refurbished program with prices starting at $499. more…
fullText:
After outing its Pixel 7 series in recent weeks, Google has just quietly released the Pixel 9 series to its Certified Refurbished program with prices starting at $499. 

Released in 2024, the Pixel 9 series introduced the updated design language we see today in Google Pixel phones, as well as continuing to improve the Tensor chipset inside. This generation also saw new camera sensors and the introduction of two Pro-tier devices – Pixel 9 Pro as a smaller 6.3-inch device, and Pixel 9 Pro XL as a bigger 6.8-inch device.

Pricing originally started at $799, but is now down to $499 as a part of Google’s Certified Refurbished program.

Google kicked off this program in late 2024 and has since shuffled around its offerings to include newer devices and remove ones that are outdated and nearing their end-of-life status for software updates. The most recent removal, as mentioned, was the Pixel 7 series in early September 2026.

	

Today sees Google releasing the Pixel 9 series (minus the Fold) to its Certified Refurbished portal on the Google Store. 

Pixel 9: $499 (Obsidian)

Pixel 9 Pro: $649 (Obsidian & Hazel)

Pixel 9 Pro XL: $699 (Obsidian & Hazel)

The base Pixel 9 is currently out of stock, but Pro and Pro XL configurations are available. Google is also throwing in a 6-month AI Plus subscription for buyers of these refurbished Pixel 9 devices:

Purchase a refurbished Pixel Pro and receive a 6-month trial of Google AI Plus with 2TB of secure storage. Smart AI and extra savings. New subscribers only, subscription voided if returned, ends 4/4/2027, terms apply.

Google’s Certified Refurbished program for Pixel phones includes a “multi-point test,” a one-year warranty, repairs using authentic Google parts, and a fully unlocked device capable of using any carrier.

title: Apple launches a new Apple TV 4K with Siri AI and remote-free voice commands
snippet: The new Apple TV 4K costs $299, comes with Siri AI, and will be available on November 13.
fullText:
Image Credits:Apple	

	

						

6:16 AM PDT · October 13, 2026

											

			

Apple launched a new $299 Apple TV 4K streaming device today, with an upgraded chip, integration with the updated version of Siri AI for content discovery, and mics that allow users to issue voice commands directly without using the remote. 

The refreshed Apple TV 4K comes with an upgraded A19 chip to enable various AI features. Hardware-wise, the new streaming box comes with three far-field microphones, letting users talk with Siri without a remote or a paired HomePod.

The company said that users can now have a four-speaker surround sound experience with Apple TV 4K  and HomePod mini 2 or HomePod 2 speakers. 

The remote also gets a welcome update: It now includes a small speaker. This helps users find the remote easily when it gets lost in the nooks and corners of the couch or when they leave the remote in another room while doing a chore. (Apple added a way to find the remote with Siri and Find My in 2023, but it hinged on showing directions in the app rather than an audible sound.)

With Siri AI now rolling out to all Apple platforms, the big draw for Apple is to utilize it for better personalization and content recommendations. On the Apple TV, viewers can ask questions like “Which Apple TV shows won at the Emmy Awards this year?” to search for content, or ask for more information about shows with questions like “Where was ‘Pluribus’ filmed?”

Rivals Google and Amazon have also added AI for content suggestions in the past few years.

The device is not updated as often as other Apple hardware, given this long-pending upgrade comes four years after the launch of Apple TV 4K in 2022. Bloomberg reported that the company wanted to launch the new device in 2024, but delays in launching the AI-powered Siri forced Apple to push the launch of new home devices as well.

Consumers can preorder the new Apple TV 4K starting today, and the device will be available on November 13.

title: Apple announces HomePod mini 2: Siri AI, new colors, Sound Glow, more
snippet: Apple has officially announced the new HomePod mini 2 smart speaker. The new product was announced by Apple today alongside the new HomeView smart display and fourth-gen Apple TV 4K. more…
fullText:
Apple has officially announced the new HomePod mini 2 smart speaker. The new product was announced by Apple today alongside the new HomeView smart display and fourth-gen Apple TV 4K.

HomePod mini 2 now available to pre-order

HomePod mini 2 features the same design as the original version. It comes in a variety of refreshed and returning color options: green, pink, blue, midnight, and white. It replaces the dated S5 chip with a new S10 chip to deliver new features and experiences.

Siri AI and Sound Glow are new to HomePod mini 2

Apple says the new HomePod mini 2 will work with Siri AI, Apple’s upgraded version of the personal assistant that debuted with iOS 27.

Powered by an entirely new architecture built on the latest generation of Apple Foundation Models, Siri AI transforms the HomePod mini experience and helps users get more done than ever before.

When paired with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad, HomePod mini can tap into a user’s personal context to help them find what they need in the moment. 

	

HomePod mini 2 also includes a new hardware feature called Sound Glow:

With Sound Glow, the top of HomePod mini transforms into a visual canvas that glows and pulses in sync with the music, reacting in real time to bass and treble. The song’s album artwork from Now Playing generates a color-matched light experience that’s unique to every song, and users can pick a soundscape like rain to trigger bespoke animations for a soothing atmosphere.

HomePod mini 2 can create a home theater experience

When paired with the new Apple TV 4K (fourth-gen), a pair of HomePod mini 2 speakers and a pair of full-size HomePod 2 speakers can create a new home theater experience as well:

HomePod mini delivers rich 360-degree sound from its compact footprint, whether it’s used as a single speaker, in a stereo pair, or as part of a multiroom audio setup. Powered by the Apple S10 chip and advanced computational audio, it analyzes music in real time to optimize dynamic range, loudness, and acoustic performance. For the first time, users can create a four-speaker surround sound experience with Apple TV 4K (4th generation) and HomePod mini 2. Together, the four speakers and the new Apple TV 4K intelligently recognize each speaker’s position in the room, so audio timing and levels are automatically calibrated to the space.

Price and availability

Pre-orders start today ahead of the launch on October 30. The price is $149. Apple says it will run “HomePod software 27.2.” Apple adds that Siri AI will come in a future software update, suggesting it may not be available at launch.

The original HomePod mini was released in November 2020 for $99. Apple increased the price to $129 earlier this year.

fullText:
One of the Pixel Watch 5’s quietly powerful features has landed on the Pixel Watch 4. The AI watch face generator that launched last year is currently rolling out to Pixel Watch 4 models.

The Pixel Watch 5 wasn’t a massive shakeup as much as another refinement. The Pixel Watch 4 brought arguably more to the table when it launched last year, but if the newest model did anything new, it was to add a few enhancements under the hood. One good byproduct of that push is an AI watch face generator; it’s a tool that makes creating custom watch faces a little easier, especially if you’re the type to pick a different one for each day of the week.

According to a few users on Reddit, a recent Pixel Watch 4 update added the AI watch face generator to their device. It looks like the update is packaged in version 4.2.12.989940186 and includes Pixel Watch 5 stock watch faces – Weave, Modular, Reveal, and Chronograph – and even the specialized Steph Curry dial. 

	

The custom face generator is straightforward. You can access the prompt section through the Pixel Watch app when you try to create a new look. Instead of picking from a template gallery, explain what you’re looking to generate, and Gemini Intelligence should come up with something close.

It has its limitations, of course, but it’s a great tool that Google didn’t really play up for the Pixel Watch 5. That made this Pixel Watch 4 update somewhat expected, but it’s a nice surprise nonetheless.

The Pixel Watch 4 update looks to be actively rolling out, so it might take some time for it to show up.
