title: Google Labs announces ‘Playground’ for prompt-based game creation
snippet: Google today announced an “experimental gaming platform” called Playground that lets you “create, play, and share” browser-based games. The goal is to “make game creation more approachable and ignite everyday creativity.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced an “experimental gaming platform” called Playground that lets you “create, play, and share” browser-based games. The goal is to “make game creation more approachable and ignite everyday creativity.”

This Google Labs experiment leverages  Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria models with a “custom harness to make game creation more accessible.”

It starts with a chat interface that lets you “direct the game just by typing what you want to build.” You can decide between a 2D or 3D game and specify whether it’s single or multi-player. Google offers starter prompts that you can remix and a guided development experience.

Playground lets you “tweak the physics, rewrite the rules, customize the characters, or overhaul the environment.”

	

Google today also previewed a Unity Spark integration that allows for “robust, professional-level mechanics, high-fidelity 3D capabilities, and the flexibility of the Unity runtime.”

The accessibility of Playground and world-class game-building expertise of Unity provides the building blocks for an ecosystem where users can start with a simple text prompt and eventually grow into building immersive experiences with Unity

These are browser-based games that are playable on phone or laptop. Once you’re done, games can be kept private, shared via link, or published to the Playground Explore gallery for everyone. Titles go through safety (community guideline) screening along with user reporting.

Players can rate games, while there’s support for in-game leaderboards with Play Games profile integration.

Google is rolling out Playground starting in the US. Free users will be able to generate games, with expanded access tied to Google One membership.

title: The Fitbit Air Is Getting an Upgrade
snippet: These are all the new features you can expect to see with the Air.
fullText:
Google is all about freshness for fall. In addition to announcing the new Fitbit Edge on Monday, the company also has three new features coming to its Fitbit Air, first released in May.

1. Health Guardian 

There’s Health Guardian, Google’s proactive health and safety tools, available in the Google Health app. It works in the background to monitor your body’s health and wellness signals, provides a monthly summary of your health indicators and trends and sends timely notifications for anything that requires your immediate attention.

		

			

Health Guardian features 

In the free Google Health app, Health Guardian includes irregular heart rhythm notifications and high and low heart rate notifications. With the Pixel Watch 3 and up, you also get loss-of-pulse notifications.

In the Premium version, which costs $10 monthly or $100 yearly, you can access these newer features: insulin resistance levels, blood pressure trends and sleep breathing quality trends. They work with the Pixel Watch 3 and up and the Fitbit Air.

Health Guardian will also come to the new Fitbit Edge, though we don’t have a specific date yet. 

Health Guardian passively tracks your health 24/7. Google

Insulin resistance

Insulin resistance refers to when your body doesn’t respond to insulin the way it should. Produced by your pancreas, insulin regulates your body’s glucose levels, moving glucose from your blood into your cells so that it can be used for energy. 

Google Health’s insulin resistance doesn’t rely on readings from a continuous glucose monitor or lab work. Instead, it uses sensors on the Pixel Watch 3 and up and Fitbit Air to estimate insulin resistance and monitor shifts in your metabolic health. 

Specifically, heart rhythm, sleep quality and daily activity data are tracked to give a user an idea of how efficiently their body absorbs energy from food and manages that energy during their activities. 

Note that insulin resistance isn’t intended to monitor real-time glucose levels, and it isn’t a prescreener for diabetes or diabetes management.

Blood pressure

Blood pressure trends rely on optical and movement sensors, pulse and motion patterns and WavesFM, Google’s own AI foundation model, to measure your pulse’s shape and speed beneath your skin. This lets it estimate blood pressure over a month and give you a summary of your heart patterns. 

However, blood pressure trends aren’t a replacement for a blood pressure monitor, so they shouldn’t be used for blood pressure management or as a prescreener for hypertension. It also isn’t designed for pregnant people.

Sleep breathing quality

For users aged 18 and up, sleep breathing quality tracks your breathing overnight to estimate how consistent and easy your breathing was during sleep. It uses your blood oxygen levels and your device’s heart rate and motion sensors. 

With sleep breathing quality, you’ll see each morning how much of your sleep was spent in optimal breathing. Then, at the end of the month, you’ll receive an assessment showing those trends. 

If you’ve been wanting better workout detection with the Fitbit Air, we have good news. Google

Remember that none of these features are for diagnosing or treating diseases. 

2. Upgraded auto-activity detection

The Fitbit Air’s automatic workout detection has been upgraded to be twice as accurate, with 50% fewer missed detections when compared to the existing version. Its large language model can now better detect your workout type based on movement, your routine, logs and location. 

For instance, it can better detect tennis and other racket sports, trail runs and HIIT. 

When she reviewed the Fitbit Air, one of CNET Principal Writer Vanessa Hand Orellana’s biggest and only criticisms of the device was that it missed low-impact workouts like Pilates, so it’s great to see that the Fitbit team paid attention to consumer feedback when revamping its workout detection. 

3. Metal mesh bands

With the Fitbit Air, you could previously choose either recycled polyester and elastane yarn bands or polyurethane bands. Now, metal mesh bands are available in silver and gold. 

The Fitbit Air’s band is also getting a style-forward makeover. Google

This makes the Air look more like jewelry and less like a fitness device. Perfect for those who prefer more discreet wearables that they can wear in any setting.

title: Fitbit Edge May Be the Sweet Spot for Smartwatch Noncommittals
snippet: Google’s new $179 tracker sits between the screenless Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5, promising some of the best parts of both without fully committing to either.
fullText:
If you’re lukewarm on smartwatches but not minimalist enough to go completely screenless, Google may have found your Goldilocks option.

The new $179 Fitbit Edge, unveiled Monday, sits between the $100 Fitbit Air and $400 Pixel Watch 5 in price, features and form factor. It gives you a color screen, built-in GPS and many of the health sensors you’d expect from a smartwatch, but in a slimmer, lighter package with up to a week of battery life.

The concept isn’t new for Fitbit. Previous trackers like the Inspire and Charge paired a simple screen with Fitbit’s health and fitness tracking while working with both iOS and Android; if anything, the screen-less Fitbit Air was the departure. But it’s been three years since the Charge 6, and Google now has a lot more to pull from across its wearable lineup. The Edge combines some of what I like about the minimalist Air with features that have trickled down from the Pixel Watch 5.

			

More from CNET

Whether that combination hits the sweet spot remains to be seen.

The Fitbit Edge is available for preorder on Monday and goes on sale Oct. 27.

The mini screen 

I’m a big fan of the minimalist Fitbit Air, which hides almost every trace of tech behind sleek bands. Aesthetically, it’s my ideal; practically, not so much. I inevitably glance down expecting to see the time, only to get annoyed at this thing seemingly freeloading on my wrist because all the payoff is in the phone app.

Apparently, I want my cake and to eat it too. That’s where the Edge comes in.

Its 1.34-inch color AMOLED display is 46% larger than the one on the Charge 6 and has an always-on option. There’s also a physical side button for pausing workouts and accessing menus.

The Edge keeps with the same style choices that make the Air and Pixel Watch 5 stand out, and as a lover of all things color, I’m here for it. It comes in Obsidian, Fog, Olive and Canyon combinations, with interchangeable options including a performance loop, magnetic band and metal links. There’s also a Stephen Curry Special Edition that costs an additional $50.

Google

Google also redesigned the interface with tiles that resemble the Pixel Watch UI, including watch faces with complications and quick access to workouts and health metrics. It still runs Fitbit’s own operating system rather than Wear OS, so this isn’t a miniature Pixel Watch as it lacks access to the Play Store and Gemini. But it does mean you can use the Fitbit Edge with the iPhone as well as Android phones.

You can get weather, alarms, timers, media controls and turn-by-turn directions. The Edge can also mirror notifications and incoming calls from your phone and send canned replies to messages on Android.

But there’s no microphone or speaker, so you can’t take calls from your wrist as you would on a smartwatch. There’s also no NFC for Google Wallet or tap-to-pay, an odd omission considering the older Charge 6 had it.

More smartwatch-like health and fitness tracking

The Edge also borrows plenty from the smartwatch side when it comes to health and fitness.

Unlike the Fitbit Air, which relies on your phone for GPS, the Edge has built-in GPS and an altimeter. It also tracks heart rate, blood oxygen and skin temperature and supports ECG readings.

Google says heart-rate tracking is 40% more accurate than on the Charge 6, a claim I’m especially interested in testing against a chest strap once I get the Edge on my wrist.

It tracks more than 50 exercise types and can automatically recognize more than 40. Google says it has also improved automatic detection since launching the Air, including the ability to recognize racquet sports.

During workouts, you can see metrics like pace and heart rate zones on your wrist, which I missed on the Air. The Edge can also broadcast live heart rate data to compatible exercise equipment, so you can see your heart rate on a treadmill or other supported machine.

The Edge comes with three months of Google Health Premium, which costs $10 per month or $100 per year after that. Premium unlocks the AI-powered Google Health Coach and Health Guardian, which measure monthly blood pressure and insulin resistance trends. Health Guardian is also coming to the Fitbit Air, but Google hasn’t said when.

Seven-day battery comes with an asterisk

Battery life is one of the Edge’s biggest advantages over a smartwatch.

Google rates it for up to seven days per charge, but there’s a massive caveat. That’s the estimate with the raise to wake setting. If you prefer an always-on display (which I do) then the estimate dwindles down to two days, according to Google. 

Google

For me, the deciding factor may be how quickly raise to wake responds. The entire reason I missed having a screen on the Air was the ability to glance down and instantly see the time. If I’m waiting for a black screen to wake up, I might as well have the Air on and just pull out my phone.

Charging is a mixed bag, too. Five minutes on the charger gets you about a day’s worth of battery, but a full charge takes about 90 minutes. Knowing my charging habits — where I don’t have a lot of downtime to recharge my wearable devices for an hour plus — I don’t need hands-on time to predict that I’ll probably never see this thing at 100%.

The Edge uses the same charger as the Air, and Google says you can move between Fitbit devices and the Pixel Watch without interrupting your health data. I can already envision a scenario where I’d use an Edge most days and swap in the Air when I forgot to charge, or want something less distracting. Whether I’d actually buy two devices to accomplish that is another question.

Fitbit’s first tracker with a user-replaceable battery

The Edge has a user-replaceable battery, making it Fitbit’s first tracker designed with this level of repairability. Google has already moved in this direction with the Pixel Watch 4, which was redesigned without adhesives to make repairs easier. My colleague Katie Collins even replaced its screen herself despite describing herself as an “ambitious amateur.”

The battery on the Fitbit Edge is replaceable. 

Bringing that approach to a smaller, less expensive tracker could help extend its life, especially since batteries inevitably degrade over time. Google says repair options vary by region and recommends self-repair only for people with the technical expertise to do it safely. 

Fitbit Edge: Bottom line 

At $179, the Edge costs nearly twice as much as the Fitbit Air and more than Fitbit’s other entry-level trackers. But compared with the Pixel Watch or Samsung’s Galaxy Watch, the price could feel like a deal if you’re prioritizing fitness features and don’t need other smartwatch features like contactless payments. For people who want GPS, a screen and notifications, and found the Air came up short, that extra money buys a lot. Few trackers this capable sell at this price: The next step up would be something like the $249 Apple Watch SE 3 or the $300 Samsung Galaxy Watch 7.

On paper, that makes the Edge a strong pick for people like me who aren’t ready to choose a smartwatch that’s only able to work with an iPhone or an Android phone. Now I need to find out whether it’s my Goldilocks wearable, or whether I’ll end up back with the smartwatch-and-band combo I once thought was my happy medium

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Vanessa Hand Orellana

title: Motorola is rolling out its Android 17 update to more devices
snippet: Motorola is expanding its Android 17 rollout, with the update making its way to many more devices including the Razr Ultra (2026) this week. more…
fullText:
Motorola is expanding its Android 17 rollout, with the update making its way to many more devices including the Razr Ultra (2026) this week. 

Motorola detailed its Android 17 update back in August, but timing details were left unclear. Now it seems to be starting to roll out in the US.

Friend-of-the-site and former (before the site was gutted last week) Managing Editor at Android Central, Derrek Lee, noticed the Android 17 update landing on his Motorola Razr Ultra (2026) this week as a 4.17GB update carrying the version number A171WLH.38-19-5. It’s still based on the September 2026 security update.

Motorola’s condensed changelog notes a “fresh, expressive design” and “smarter notifications,” both of which were detailed in a previous detailed overview of the update. 

	

Interestingly, the update has yet to land for the Motorola Razr Fold at this point, but one would imagine that’s not too far away. 

The Razr Ultra (2026) isn’t the only device being updated, though. The floodgates seem to have opened with Edge 60 Fusion, Edge 60 Pro, Motorola Signature, and more all being updated in the past few days. Edge 70 devices were updated a few weeks ago.

title: iOS 27.0.1 is now Apple’s recommended update for users still on iOS 26
snippet: Apple launched iOS 27 on September 14, but the new OS version was initially minimized in Settings while iOS 26.7 was spotlighted as the recommended update. But now following the release of iOS 27.0.1, that has officially changed. more…
fullText:
Apple launched iOS 27 on September 14, but the new OS version was initially minimized in Settings while iOS 26.7 was spotlighted as the recommended update. But now following the release of iOS 27.0.1, that has officially changed.

iPhones running iOS 26 will default to iOS 27.0.1 as next update

Over the last few years, Apple has started rolling out its major new iOS updates more gradually.

For example, while iOS 27 officially became available to all users on September 14, it wasn’t featured as the default, top-level update in the Settings app.

Instead, until very recently, users saw iOS 26.7 as the recommended update, while iOS 27 was minimized under a small ‘Also Available’ section in the Software Update screen.

Apple does this because inevitably, despite a months-long beta process, there are often new bugs that emerge following the public launch. And the company wants the chance to address these before pushing the update to its full user base.

But now with iOS 27.0.1 available, Apple has made iOS 27 the default update for users still on iOS 26.

	

So the next time those users go to Settings ⇾ General ⇾ Software Update, they’ll see iOS 27.0.1 featured prominently.

Users will still have the option of staying on iOS 26. But we can expect to see iOS 27 adoption accelerate now that Apple has made it the primary update in Settings.

Last year Apple waited until after iOS 26.1 was available before recommending the switch from iOS 18. So pushing iOS 27 much earlier this year is a clear endorsement of the company’s focus on bug fixes and stability with its latest major update.

title: Claude launches Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides integration with sidebar and more
snippet: If Gemini isn’t quite your cup of tea, Anthropic’s Claude now supports sidebar integration with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides. more…
fullText:
If Gemini isn’t quite your cup of tea, Anthropic’s Claude now supports sidebar integration with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides.

You can already use Gemini natively in Google Workspace apps, but those invested in Claude can now use their AI of choice inside of Google’s ecosystem through the Claude for Google Workspace add-on which is in public beta starting today. A sidebar opens up alongside your file in Docs, Sheets, or Slides and can assist in building out documents, making edits, and more.

In Google Docs, Anthropic says you can use Claude integration to fix spelling, rewrite portions of a document, or restyle sections, all without breaking existing formatting. In Sheets, you can have Claude write formulas or build tables using the context of the document, or even upload extra documents/spreadsheets to build something new in Sheets. In Slides, Claude can build new slides using existing layouts or themes or flag elements that might need to be updated. Gemini can do much of this but, as mentioned, this is useful for those already invested in Claude.

There’s an “ask before edits” mode where Claude will let you preview changes before they’re made.

	

The Claude for Google Workspace beta is available to all paid Claude users through the Google Workspace marketplace. There are also new Claude connectors for Docs, Sheets, and Slides that let you edit Google Workspace files directly from Claude itself just by pasting a file link into your conversation with the AI.

fullText:
Last year, Kuxiu was the first to make chargers that perfectly match the Cosmic Orange iPhone. They released their 3-in-1 X40 turbo and their S4 Solid State battery pack. They both matched the orange color so well that it seemed as if they were 1st-party accessories. This year, the new hero color for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup is burgundy, and Kuxiu is back at it again with a new matching burgundy D5 5-in-1 charging station. With its premium build quality, perfect color matching, built-in cooling, and price, this charger is everything you need from a performance and aesthetic standpoint.

Be sure to check out our hands-on video below!

Kuxiu D5 specs & features

I reviewed their original D5 a few months back, and it was one of my favorite chargers of the year. Now they have brought it all back with some awesome-looking accents and features. The Kuxiu D5 is advertised as a 5-in-1 charger because it charges three devices but also features a built-in cooling fan and a diagnostics display. You get:

Qi2.2 25W wireless charging

Retractable Apple Watch charging puck

AirPods charging mat

Built-in cooling fan that can be manually turned off and on

Smart color display to give us real-time charging stats

Includes 45W charging brick and braided cable in the packaging

While it is not as compact as something like their X40 Turbo, there is still some thought put into portability and travel with this charger. The Qi2.2 charger can fold down flat into a small cube you can take wherever you need, and the Apple Watch charger retracts into the charger as well. For me, it has worked best as a permanent desk charger, but it’s nice to know that it is also portable. 

My experience

As I mentioned, I have been using the original black color for a few months as my main desk charger. It is reliable, functional, and simple to use. So when Kuxiu announced their Burgundy version, I knew I had to check it out, especially since I was looking for some Burgundy color-matching accessories for my new iPhone 18 Pro. 

Since I knew this charger was already great, I wanted to see how closely the color matched the iPhone 18 Pro, and I was impressed by how identical it was. The aluminum parts of the D5 match the Burgundy on the iPhone 18 Pro, and they add other burgundy accents across the charger’s different materials. 

Beyond the aesthetics, my favorite part is the built-in cooling fan because it adds tangible value to the setup. I am someone who constantly installs new iOS betas, tests new features, and puts my phone through situations where it tends to get warm. So, having the active cooling system built directly into the charger has been game-changing in keeping my phone efficiently cooled and helping it sustain 25W charging for longer, since it does not get warm. The fan is also dead silent, but if you do want to turn it off, you can do so with one tap. Then, of course, you have the diagnostics display that shows you all the charging stats you need to see from all the active chargers. 

Pricing & availability

The Kuxiu D5 is available today on Kuxiu’s site in the original Space Grey and their new Burgundy color. You also get the required 45W charging brick and a braided USB-C cable. It is currently on sale for $59.99. 

Final take

For under $60, I challenge someone to find me a high-quality 3-in-1 charger that offers all the features above and includes all the charging accessories you need to use it at its best. That is why Kuxiu is one of the brands I recommend the most; it’s the performance-to-price ratio that sets them apart. So if you just picked up a new Burgundy iPhone or you are in the market for a new 3-in-1 charger, I highly recommend checking this one out. My only wish is that the next version has a USB-C port so you can charge a 4th device, like a smart ring or something. Otherwise, this thing is great.

macOS 27: What’s new for iPhone Mirroring 

The biggest change for iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now adjust the size of the iPhone Mirroring window with any iOS 27-compatible apps. Right now, that means it only works for Apple’s native iPhone apps. However, once developers start rolling out iOS 27 updates later this year, support for resizing will expand rapidly.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only support three preset sizes: smaller, actual size, and larger. The change in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27 clearly indicates Apple is prepping for the foldable iPhone Ultra, expected to launch later this year.

iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 and iOS 27 also has several other updates:

Control Center access

DRM video support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring did not support accessing Control Center at all. In macOS 27, you can access it with the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut or with the “View” menu in your Mac’s menu bar.

DRM video support means you can watch protected videos using iPhone Mirroring on your Mac. Previously, all DRM-protected videos would simply show a black screen when iPhone Mirroring was enabled.

macOS 27 also has a new app icon for iPhone Mirroring, just like it does for many other stock Apple apps.

iPhone Duo is just about two weeks away from releasing, and according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has big retail plans ahead for its first foldable iPhone, to make sure every customer gets to see it to the fullest.

Apple is gearing up for a major launch with the iPhone Duo, which should be no surprise. What is a surprise though, is the amount of attention Apple is putting into making sure this launch goes as smoothly as possible.

In the newsletter, Gurman reports that the company is planning to have over a hundred demo units at some of its biggest stores:

The company is preparing a major retail push, with a huge number of demo units at its flagship stores. The Fifth Avenue location in New York City is expected to have more than 150 units across hands-on demo stations and in-store fixtures. The Apple Park Visitor Center at the company’s home base, meanwhile, will have nearly 100. Other locations, including Michigan Avenue in Chicago, the Grove in Los Angeles and the Upper West Side in Manhattan, will each have roughly 30 to 40 units.

Some of its smaller stores will only have around 20 units, which still seems bigger than usual, given the fact that there are only two colors. Given how hard it’ll be to buy a Duo at launch, allowing a lot of hands-on demos at once seems sensible.

iPhone Duo demo fixtures

Beyond the number of demo units, the company has also designed a new MagSafe stand that can hold an unfolded iPhone Duo, alongside two “standard” iPhones (likely iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.) There’ll also be iPhone Duo demo units without a security tether “along the sides of stores,” so users can demo StandBy mode and other features.

Lastly, the company is planning a new fixture for some Apple Stores that showcase the iPhone Duo opening and closing, so it’s “impossible to miss” when you walk into an Apple Store.

All in all, iPhone Duo will become the forefront of Apple Stores after its launch on October 23rd. It’ll be hard to get, so if you’re interested in owning one – make sure you’re geared up to preorder it on October 16th.

title: Apple Home adds two powerful new features in iOS 27
snippet: Apple is launching several new Home products next week, so it’s no surprise that iOS 27 includes big upgrades in the Home app. Here are two powerful new Home features in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
Apple is launching several new Home products next week, so it’s no surprise that iOS 27 includes big upgrades in the Home app. Here are two powerful new Home features in iOS 27.

#1: HomeKit Secure Video packs big upgrades in iOS 27

HomeKit Secure Video is Apple’s secure, cloud-based service included with iCloud+ for compatible video cameras. It lets you record footage, view it from anywhere, and set up activity automations.

In iOS 27, Apple Intelligence powers three new HomeKit Secure Video upgrades (via Apple):

Generated video descriptions: “users can quickly understand what happened across a sequence of video clips, even without watching them.”

Search in clips: “[users] can easily find what they’re looking for, like a package delivery.”

Noteworthy clips: “At the top of the Search page, the Home app elevates noteworthy clips that users may want to review, so they can quickly see important moments.”

Joining these is a fourth feature, not powered by AI, that’s been on users’ wishlists for a while: 4K video. Apple says, “supported HomeKit Secure Video cameras can now stream and record in 4K.” Previously, 1080p was the max resolution.

If you’re looking for a HomeKit Secure Video-compatible camera, I’d recommend:

Aqara G100 2K security camera: Excellent budget-friendly option currently only $33

eufy 4K security camera: For 4K support if you have more to spend

#2: Real-time notification updates

Most of the Home app’s upgrades this year focus on HomeKit Secure Video. But there’s also another AI-powered new feature: real-time updating notifications.

Here’s how Apple describes it:

The Home app draws on Apple Intelligence to understand related notifications as a single activity, so users receive one notification that updates as the activity happens.

Inside a new Apple Intelligence section of the Home app’s settings screen, you’ll see a ‘Reduce Notifications’ toggle. It explains: “Combine related activities, such as someone arriving and unlocking the door, in one notification that updates in real time.”

Essentially, Home app notifications will stop showing outdated information, and only focus on the latest, most relevant info.

So instead of seeing the seven related notifications above, you’ll get one alert that says: ”Lydia arrived. Checked the mail. Garage Door was closed.”

title: The 2026 Startup Battlefield Top 20: From organs to orbit and everything in between
snippet: Twenty founders just earned their shot at Disrupt glory. They're headed to the main stage at TechCrunch Disrupt to compete for the $100,000 prize and the coveted Disrupt Cup.
fullText:
Twenty founders just earned their shot at Disrupt glory. They’re headed to the Disrupt Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt to compete for the $100,000 prize and the coveted Disrupt Cup.

Every year, thousands of founders from around the world pitch us on what they believe the future should look like. This year’s Top 20 are building it from organs to orbit and everywhere in between.

Across this cohort, one theme kept emerging: Making the previously invisible measurable.

These founders are finding ways to understand signals we couldn’t previously capture, model systems too complex to predict, and turn the physical world into data that machines can actually act on. They’re measuring the biological clocks inside our bodies and growing miniature human organs in labs. They’re teaching robots to take on increasingly complex physical work and modeling the real world closely enough to predict what might happen next — even the behavior of wild animals. They’re extracting intelligence from scam calls and finding new ways to use the computing power already orbiting above our heads.

And then, of course, there’s the company trying to launch cargo into space with a giant hydrogen-powered cannon.

Subtle, this group is not.

What connects these 20 companies isn’t a single technology or industry. It’s an ambition to understand more of the world around us — biological, physical, industrial, and digital — and use that understanding to make better decisions, automate what once required human intervention, and tackle problems that previously seemed too complex to solve.

Now they have six minutes on the Disrupt Stage to prove it.

Here are the 2026 Startup Battlefield Top 20.

Tuesday, October 13 

Startup Battlefield Semifinals Session 1 (10:00 a.m. – 11:15 a.m.)

Space and Physical AI 

Longshot Space: Reinventing the economics of space by launching cargo to orbit at $50/kg using hydrogen-powered kinetic launchers.

Veritas: Protecting luxury brands with custom microchips that verify authenticity and enable connected post-purchase experiences.

Laplace Intelligence: Building agentic world models that help cities, ports, and airports roll out counterfactual futures of the real world before they act.

Flox Intelligence: Preventing deadly wildlife collisions at airports and railways with real-time AI that detects animal behavior and safely redirects them.

Satlyt: Helping satellite operators unlock and monetize idle compute by transforming their spacecraft into virtual AI data centers with a single line of code.

Battlefield Semifinal Session 2 (1:00 p.m. – 2:15 p.m.)

Energy and Manufacturing

LNK Energies: Delivering clean hydrogen power cheaper than diesel through breakthrough compact reactor technology compatible with existing diesel infrastructure.

Helix Carbon: Helping steelmakers cut emissions and fuel costs by electrochemically upcycling blast furnace waste gas into replacement fossil fuels on-site.

IndustrialNext: Automating high-precision, contact-rich assembly tasks by deploying AI-driven robotic systems that learn from production data and adapt to new products.

Niobia AI: Helping process and materials engineers compress weeks of root-cause analysis into minutes with domain-expert AI reasoning.

Licube: Producing ultra-high purity lithium and lithium isotopes (Li-6/Li-7), the critical inputs for nuclear fusion and advanced materials.

Wednesday, October 14 

Battlefield Semifinal Session 3 (10:00 a.m. – 11:15 a.m.)

Health Tech and Life Sciences 

Mosqitter: Detecting and preventing mosquito-borne disease spread with real-time disease intelligence platforms that turn sensor networks into early warning systems for national health agencies.

Hiyd AI: Delivering proactive health insights by combining sleep, movement, and nutrition data through an ultra-slim, discreet wearable tracker and AI app.

TimeTeller GmbH: Measuring people’s biological clocks to determine optimal treatment timing through molecular diagnostics and AI, improving efficacy and reducing side effects.

NTangible: Helping coaches and front offices make smarter recruiting decisions by quantifying how athletes perform under pressure with a validated cognitive score.

Intero Biosystems: Accelerating drug development by producing miniature human organs that enable pharma companies to identify safer, more effective medications while reducing clinical trial costs.

Battlefield Semifinal Session 4 (1:30 p.m. – 2:45 p.m.)

Enterprise and Security

Apate.ai: Dismantling scam operations by deploying conversational AI bots that engage scammers and turn their interactions into real-time intelligence for banks, telcos, and governments.

CedarDB: Delivering the data layer for the AI age — real-time transactions and analytics in one engine with guardrails inside the database system that AI agents can’t bypass.

Prismm: Helping banks retain deposits and relationships across generations by automating secure inheritance workflows and financial continuity infrastructure.

Floqer: Streamlining B2B sales by enriching customer data across 80+ sources and stitching every interaction into one millisecond-retrievable timeline for AI agents to act on.

GUDEA: Delivering immediate, actionable insights into audience behavior, engagement patterns, and how information spreads to give organizations a competitive edge in communication management.

And then there were five

After four semifinal sessions across two days, five companies will advance to the Startup Battlefield Finals on Thursday, October 15.

Before the finalists take the stage at 11:30 a.m., we’ll welcome Glīd, Nephrogen, and Molecule.one back to the Disrupt Stage for an alumni update on what’s happened since their time in Startup Battlefield.

Then, at 4:15 p.m., one company will be crowned the 2026 Startup Battlefield champion, taking home $100,000 and the Disrupt Cup.

Feeling the FOMO? It’s not too late. Grab a last-minute Disrupt ticket for 50% off and watch it all unfold live.

title: Where Google Wallet state IDs are available on Android
snippet: States across the US are slowly rolling out support for adding your driver’s license or ID to the Google Wallet app on Android. more…
fullText:
States across the US are slowly rolling out support for adding your driver’s license or ID to the Google Wallet app on Android.

Update 10/10

How to add your state ID on Android

Open the Google Wallet app on Android 9+

Tap the “plus” button next to “View more” at the bottom

Choose “ID & personal info” and then “Driver’s license or state ID” 

Select your state and follow the instructions

The process involves taking a picture of the front and back of your physical card, as well as a short video of yourself for verification: a “photo from this video will be submitted to your ID issuer.” 

Once approved, the ID will appear below the carousel of payment methods alongside other passes. The order can be rearranged, while you can remotely remove the ID online if your phone is missing: myaccount.google.com > Personal Info > Manage IDs.

	

Related: Google Wallet rolling out stacked card list redesign on Android

What Google Wallet state IDs are supported

Arizona (Rolled out October 2023)

Arkansas (Rolled out October 2025)

California (Rolled out August 2024)

Colorado (Rolled out October 2023)

Georgia (Rolled out October 2023)

Iowa (Rolled out June 2025)

Maryland (Rolled out December 2022)

Montana (Rolled out August 2025)

New Mexico (Rolled out December 2024)

North Dakota (Rolled out October 2025)

Ohio (Rolled out September 2026)

[New] Oklahoma (Rolled out October 2026)

Puerto Rico (Rolled out October 2025)

Where state IDs are coming next

Google previously said to expect support in the following places:

West Virginia (Upcoming availability announced April 2025)

Where you can use state IDs

The primary place you can use this digital ID is at TSA checkpoints in some US airports. There are two ways to do so, starting with tapping your phone at the NFC terminal. You then review the information that will be shared with the TSA and authenticate with device unlock. There’s also a QR code method that requires opening the ID in Google Wallet. 

Officially, you still have to carry the physical ID card at all times.

Some apps, like from car rental services, are beginning to accept digital IDs for identity and age verification. On mobile, if an app or website requests your age, it’s as simple as confirming (and authenticating) that you want to share this information with a system-level prompt/sheet. On desktop web, the experience involves scanning a QR code. 

Google wants to make it possible to do that “without any possibility to link back to a user’s personal identity” through what it calls Zero-Knowledge Proof. This technology will be open-sourced for anyone to use. 

Looking ahead, the IDs can be used at DMVs in Arizona, Georgia, Maryland, and New Mexico as part of “improved and streamlined customer experiences.”

	

Google is also working on letting you use digital IDs to “recover Amazon accounts, access online health services with CVS and MyChart by Epic, verify profiles on platforms like Uber and more.”

Using passport as REAL ID

Google in April pointed out how you can “use your ID pass created from a U.S. passport with TSA security for domestic travel at supported airports, even if you do not have a REAL ID driver’s license or state-issued ID.” This comes ahead of the May 7, 2025 deadline. 

To do so, open Google Wallet > Add to Wallet > ID pass. This three-step process involves taking a picture of your passport’s info page, and then scanning the security chip found inside the back cover of your passport. You also have to record a video of your face that Google will review “to make sure you’re a real person, and compare the video to your passport photo to make sure you’re the owner of the passport.”

The NFC and QR code instructions for using this digital passport ID are unchanged from above. You also have to keep the physical version on you when traveling. As a reminder, this won’t work internationally.

title: Amazon’s new Alexa Tablet finally gives the iPad lineup some much needed competition
snippet: This week, Amazon unveiled a new lineup of Alexa Tablets. They no longer run a proprietary OS with a custom App Store, and instead embrace Android with a stock feel – while offering the Play Store. It’s a big shift in direction for Amazon. The tablets also look quite beautiful, while previous Fire tablets have felt cheap. I think these have the opportunity to do quite well. more…
fullText:
This week, Amazon unveiled a new lineup of Alexa Tablets. They no longer run a proprietary OS with a custom App Store, and instead embrace Android with a stock feel – while offering the Play Store. It’s a big shift in direction for Amazon. The tablets also look quite beautiful, while previous Fire tablets have felt cheap. I think these have the opportunity to do quite well.

First and foremost, I want to make it quite clear that I’m not saying the iPad is doomed or anything remotely close to that. However, I do think the Alexa Tablet serves as a real form of iPad competition, which the iPad has generally lacked.

New Alexa tablets serve as strong competition

Amazon is putting a lot of care into these tablets that other Android manufacturers haven’t, and while these tablets come in at lower price points – they certainly punch above their weight class.

There are three Alexa Tablets to start off the lineup: an 8.7” model at $229, an 11” model at $329, and a 12” Pro model at $499. To me, the one in the middle is the most interesting.

It offers 8GB of RAM, a 90Hz display, a thin design, and a similarly sharp display. That compares to the budget iPad, which comes in $120 higher with less RAM, a lesser display, and a thicker design. Granted, the iPad has the A16 chip, which probably feels much faster than the MediaTek chip powering it. The iPad also starts at 128GB, compared to the 64GB on the Alexa Tablet. Once you upgrade the Alexa Tablet to 128GB, there’s only a $70 difference.

Hardware wise, the Alexa Tablets seem pretty competent. Obviously, Android on tablets isn’t going to be quite perfect, but given its tie in with Alexa and the fact that the tablet is priced quite well, I could see a lot of people wanting to buy these, even if they potentially would’ve considered iPads. Of course, one strong suit from Amazon is the Kindle experience, and these Alexa Tablets offer a reader mode that cuts blue light.

Wrap up

Only time will tell, but Amazon might make a pretty big dent into the tablet market with its new entries. Even the 12” Pro at $499 seems like a really worthwhile product. At the very least, I hope some strong competition means Apple will be less complacent with its iPad upgrades. For example, the iPad Air has largely only received chip upgrades since its last redesign in 2020.

	

I’m personally excited to try one of these out and truly put it to the test. Right now, Amazon also offers 20% off with any trade-in, making it an even better deal.

What do you think of these new Alexa Tablets? Would you consider getting one of these for a friend or family member during the holiday season? Sound off in the comments.

title: watchOS 27 adds three new apps to your Apple Watch
snippet: watchOS 27 is the latest major software update for Apple Watch, and among its variety of new features, it adds three new apps to your Watch. more…
fullText:
watchOS 27 is the latest major software update for Apple Watch, and among its variety of new features, it adds three new apps to your Watch.

#1: Siri

Siri just got a major AI overhaul in watchOS 27, and one part of that is a brand new Siri app.

The Siri app is available across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Vision Pro, and also the Apple Watch.

watchOS 27 still lets you invoke Siri via the Digital Crown, but the app is another place you can go to start a conversation. Perhaps more importantly, the app is where you can browse past ones.

Siri AI is more conversational than the old assistant, and keeps a record of past queries across all your devices. So the Siri app in watchOS 27 shows you conversations not just from your Apple Watch, but from your iPhone, Mac, and more.

#2: Find My

Joining iOS 27’s new features for the Find My app, Apple has rethought the Find My experience in watchOS this year too.

In watchOS 26, Find My was split up into three separate apps: Find Devices, Find Items, and Find People.

But in watchOS 27, Apple has streamlined all finding features into a new, unified ‘Find My’ app.

Find My on Apple Watch provides all the functionality of the previous three apps, but in a condensed experience so you can easily locate anything or anyone on a map-centric view.

You can switch between different things you’re looking for via a menu in the top-left corner, but otherwise you’ll see a consistent interface.

#3: Readiness

If you own an Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4, watchOS 27 also adds a third app: Readiness.

Here’s what the Readiness app does, per the App Store:

The Readiness app analyzes your recent activity, vitals, and sleep to help you understand your capacity to take on the day.

Features

Get a score and a clear classification of your readiness, including Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready, or Go For It.

See an explanation of relevant factors and tap through to associated apps.

Add complications and Smart Stack widgets for convenient and glanceable insights.

View additional details in the Fitness app on iPhone.

Essentially, Readiness provides you a quick glimpse into your overall vitals so you know how well rested and ready your body may be on a given day.

title: Gemini ‘Task’ redesign integrates Spark into the main chat app
snippet: In addition to revamping settings and the navigation drawer, Google is combining its Spark personal agent with the main Gemini chat experience. more…
fullText:
In addition to revamping settings and the navigation drawer, Google is combining its Spark personal agent with the main Gemini chat experience.

This redesign adds buttons for “Chat” and “Task” just above the prompt box. “Task” is Gemini Spark, with Google explaining that there’s now a “new home for Spark: Start new tasks anytime and keep track of them in your chats.”

Old vs. new

As part of this change, “Spark” disappears from the navigation drawer, while a new “Scheduled” page is introduced. This surfaces Spark tasks and Scheduled actions, with the feed organized by Active, Paused, Completed, and Suggested. 

	

Meanwhile, the list of conversations at the bottom is no longer called Recents. All chats and Spark tasks are combined into one history. The new filter icon lets you sort by All, Ready, Needs attention, and In progress.

Google appears to be deemphasizing the “Spark” branding with this redesign. Another example is how “Gemini Spark Settings” in the account menu has been renamed to just “Task settings.” 

This change is rolling out via a server-side update on Android. We’re not seeing it just yet on iOS or the web. Gemini Spark requires an AI Pro or AI Ultra subscription.

Announced at I/O 2026 in May, Gemini’s 24/7 personal agent is now better integrated into the overall app with this update. It’s much quicker to start a task with the experience no longer siloed off.

title: Cyberattack Targets French Supermarket Refrigerators, Forcing Mass Food Disposal
snippet: Hackers took advantage of a software vulnerability, proving again that any connected appliance on the internet can be a target.
fullText:
Hundreds of supermarkets in France were the subject of a coordinated hack early Monday morning that turned up the heat on fridges and freezers, causing food to spoil and, in some cases, fires to break out.

According to reports from AFP, three major grocery chains in the country — E. Leclerc, Intermarche and Cooperative U — reported that hackers forced connected fridges and freezers at hundreds of stores to go into defrost mode for several hours, raising their temperatures to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit). Paris authorities told the news agency that other grocery chains were also hit.

While it’s unclear who is responsible for the attacks or the exact exploit chain used, the hackers targeted software on two Danfoss system controllers. The company told the industry publication Cooling Post that the affected systems, AK-SM800 and AK-SC355, were running outdated firmware. “We are working with affected customers to implement appropriate mitigation measures, including firmware updates where available, stronger network protections and removing direct internet exposure where applicable,” Danfoss told Cooling Post.

			

More from CNET

On a web page for its AK-SM800 controllers, Danfoss says the company “takes security seriously” and that “new measures are being implemented” to improve security. 

A representative for Danfoss didn’t immediately return a request for comment.

The incidents are alarming for several reasons. In addition to proving yet again that network-connected devices, especially older ones, can be targets of attack, the French supermarket attack highlights vulnerabilities in global food supplies that can be quickly and dangerously exploited.

Dominique Schelcher, CEO of Cooperative U, said in a post on X that an investigation into the attack is underway. “Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented,” he posted (translated from French). 

Je confirme qu’une cyberattaque touche depuis cette nuit les installations de production de froid de plusieurs magasins de notre réseau @CooperativeU.

Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées, en lien avec les frigoristes, pour rétablir la situation au plus vite. Une enquête devra…

— Dominique Schelcher (@schelcher) October 12, 2026

The ‘internet of things’ is being attacked

The attack on a French supermarket underscores the growing risk of attacks on operational technology and cold-chain infrastructure. Though the fridges and freezer units weren’t consumer smart fridges with app controls and touch screens, the controllers were connected to the internet to remotely manage defrost cycles, temperatures and alarms across many stores. 

Companies may have many reasons for using these kinds of OT devices. They can log temperatures to ensure they’re meeting food safety standards, deploy firmware updates to prevent security incidents like this one and get alerts if a fridge or freezer is malfunctioning. Some devices like this also monitor inventory or even update prices for digital shelf displays.

But just as appliances from companies such as Samsung can be affected by a hack or even software glitches — like a recent incident in Korea that bricked some smart fridges — these industrial devices rely on imperfect software and internet connections, which expose them to the outside world.

Older IT and operational systems that are incorporated into connected systems may be especially difficult to defend, said Nathaniel Jones, senior vice president of global threat intelligence at Darktrace. “A cyber incident no longer affects only data or business systems; it can manipulate physical equipment and cause real-world damage.”

That damage can scale quickly if those systems are spread across many locations, all of which are exposed to the internet. “If it is connected, it can be targeted,” Jones said in a statement to CNET via email.

If that’s not scary enough, these are the same types of vulnerabilities that can make utilities such as power grids, water suppliers and even nuclear power plants vulnerable to attack.

title: Google Cloud announces ‘Gemini agent’ as ‘universal agent for work’
snippet: At Gemini at Work 2026, Google Cloud today announced the “Gemini agent” for enterprise customers. more…
fullText:
At Gemini at Work 2026, Google Cloud today announced the “Gemini agent” for enterprise customers.

Gemini agent is a “new single, universal agent for work” available in the Gemini Enterprise app, Workspace, and third-party services. Google says you can “give it objectives, not instructions.” It can answer questions, handle knowledge work, create media, and write/run code.

“For example, if your manager emails you asking for the latest project update as a slide deck, Workspace Intelligence recognizes that as a delegatable task and gives you a single-click option to pass it to Gemini.”

…you can ask Gemini to set up a meeting with the usual team of regional event leads next week, without supplying a single name or email address. Gemini determines who those people are from the membership of your chat space and the thread from your last event, checks their calendars, and starts an email thread to coordinate a time that works, even with external participants.

Besides functioning as a personal assistant, the Gemini agent can serve as a “team member, where it works on behalf of a group of people, like a project manager within a team, or on behalf of a specific role in an organization, like an analyst in your finance department.”

	

Under-the-hood, the Gemini agent “runs each job on the model that fits best.” This includes both the Gemini and Claude families of models today with support for other private and open models in the future. This is meant to “deliver optimal quality and lower your costs.” It uses sub-agents to “tackle multi-step tasks” and connects with various third-party tools. 

	

Gemini can communicate with these sub-agents to coordinate workflows, including parallel and sequential steps that can run for hours or days.

The agent runs in the cloud for a “single set of memories, context, and one personalization graph.” There are four kinds of memory: 

Session memory: “for the task in front of it, even when it runs for days”

Semantic memory: “a structured knowledge base it builds as it reads documents, talks to people, and works with other agents”

Procedural memory: “for how a job gets done, including skills it writes for itself:

Episodic memory: “everything it has done before”

In Gmail, Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Chat, you can mention @Gemini to invoke. The Gemini agent is available from any device and channel, with command line, Google Workspace, Slack, and Microsoft 365 given as examples. An API allows it to be integrated into third-party applications to surface and operate as a “headless agent, meaning it does not need a dedicated user interface.”

The Gemini agent will see wide availability soon for Workspace customers with select Business and Enterprise plans. It’s currently in private preview.

Typically, Apple’s fall updates for IT are around better way to manage devices, etc. This year, there was an underrated update that I think will be a real win in certain situations: remote AppleCare log collection.

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers has been an Apple IT admin since 2009. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade WiFi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, share stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

If you’ve ever opened an AppleCare support case for a hard-to-reproduce issue in your Apple fleet, you know how hard this process is. AppleCare needed a sysdiagnose and getting one meant either physically having the device or walking a user through a series of steps they’ve never done before. That process worked eventually, but it was slow, required the user to be available and willing to help, and, for remote employees or traveling executives, made it appear that IT didn’t have sufficient visibility into the logs of what was happening on the devices. The issue is that they somewhat didn’t.

The harder the issue was to reproduce, the more frustrating this was for IT. By the time you got the logs, the device had rebooted, the macOS state had changed, and you were starting over with your troubleshooting.

TriggerEnhancedLogCollection is your friend

Apple introduced two new device management commands in iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS 27: TriggerEnhancedLogCollection and a cancel command. The process is straightforward. You open an AppleCare case, AppleCare provides you a token, and you pass that token through your device management when you trigger the command. The device collects the logs and uploads them directly to Apple, where they are automatically attached to the ticket with Apple.

The device also reports its status through declarative management at all times, so you can see whether log collection has started, whether it’s finished, whether it’s waiting on user consent, and if the upload is in progress. 

Interactive vs non-interactive

There are two modes for this command, and the difference matters depending on what you’re managing. On iOS, non-interactive mode is available when the device has no passcode and no accounts, so it collects and uploads logs in the background without user involvement. I think this would be applicable in kiosk/POS type settings. On tvOS and Shared iPads, non-interactive is always available.

On macOS, interactive mode is required. The user sees a notification and is prompted to consent to both the log collection and the upload. They can decline, but this is still dramatically better than the old process, but it’s not completely hands-off. The user is in the loop., but at least it’s a simple UI box..

Wrap up

Remote and hybrid work make manual log collection harder and a remote user in a different city experiencing intermittent macOS issues is one of the more challenging support scenarios an IT team can face. With this feature, the moment that Apple’s team asks for logs, you can send the command from your device management console, the device does the work, and Apple has the info it needs to work the case.

title: TrendForce warns of higher notebook prices and weaker demand in 2027
snippet: TrendForce projects that global notebook shipments could decline by a high-single-digit percentage in 2027, depending on how manufacturers respond to rising component costs. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
TrendForce projects that global notebook shipments could decline by a high-single-digit percentage in 2027, depending on how manufacturers respond to rising component costs. Here are the details.

’Brands [to] face difficult trade-offs’

In a report released this week, TrendForce projects that global notebook shipments will decline in 2027, with the drop ranging from low- to high-single digits, depending on how manufacturers respond to rising costs.

TrendForce says the impact will depend on how much of the rising component costs manufacturers pass on to consumers through higher retail prices, rather than absorbing them at the expense of their profit margins.

From the report:

TrendForce’s latest notebook industry research reveals that the primary risk facing the market in 2027 is expected to shift from supply constraints to the impact of rising costs on demand. Global notebook shipments are currently projected to decline by a low-single-digit percentage in 2027.

However, if DRAM and CPU prices remain elevated, brands may be forced to pass more of these costs on to consumers. These higher retail prices could further extend replacement cycles, potentially pushing the full-year shipment decline into the high-single-digit range.

TrendForce says that notebook shipments in 2026 were supported by factors such as improved CPU availability, early purchasing by manufacturers, and replacement demand brought forward from later periods.

With some purchases originally expected in the second half of 2026 and beyond already brought forward, replacement momentum in subsequent periods is likely to weaken. Furthermore, as lower-cost inventories are gradually depleted, brands will face more direct pressure from rising CPU, DRAM, and SSD prices.

The report notes that 68% of the bill of materials for an unnamed “mainstream notebook with a manufacturer’s suggested retail price of US$900” was made up of CPU, DRAM, and SSD costs in the third quarter of 2026.

	

It adds that next year, if component costs keep rising, brands will likely have to choose between raising retail prices and risking weaker demand, absorbing the increases at the expense of gross margins, or reducing specifications, potentially making their products less competitive.

TrendForce says that DRAM supply is “likely to stay tight” next year thanks to AI-related demand, “while PC DRAM faces the risk of limited supply growth.” On the flip side, it expects NAND Flash supply constraints to “ease in the second half of 2027 with new capacity coming online. “

In 2027, brands are therefore unlikely to be able to maintain pricing, specifications, and profitability simultaneously. The extent to which they pass higher costs on to consumers will be a key factor shaping demand.

Finally, the report notes that if tariff pressures don’t increase further, manufacturers could move some notebook production back to China to reduce costs. TrendForce estimates that China’s share of global notebook production will rise from 76% in 2025 to 79% in 2026, potentially exceeding 80% in 2027.

title: iPhone Duo buyers to get a special surprise at U.S. Apple Stores, report says
snippet: According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, iPhone Duo buyers who purchase their device at an Apple Store in the US will be treated to a nice little surprise when they turn it on for the first time. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, iPhone Duo buyers who purchase their device at an Apple Store in the US will be treated to a nice little surprise when they turn it on for the first time. Here are the details.

Cool surprise in store for in-store buyers

When Apple launches the iPhone Duo on October 23, some customers who purchase the device at an Apple Store in the US will be able to have its initial setup screen personalized with their name.

According to Gurman, “Apple retail stores will have a system to customize the boot of the device,” allowing the iPhone Duo to display a greeting containing their name when it turns on for the first time. Gurman says the feature will be exclusive to the iPhone Duo, and support both English and Spanish.

Fun little touch for the iPhone Duo launch: Apple retail stores will have a system to customize the boot of the device with the buyer's name so it says "Hello, Mark" (for example) when it turns on for the first time. (US only, Duo only, English and Spanish).

— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) October 9, 2026

It is not clear how Apple will implement the feature, or whether it will rely on Presto, the system Apple Stores already use to wirelessly update iPhones without removing them from their boxes.

	

First reported by Gurman in 2023, Presto allows Apple retail employees to turn on an iPhone, install software updates, and turn it off again, all while the device remains sealed in its packaging.

Back to the iPhone Duo, it will be available to pre-order starting Friday, October 16, with deliveries and in-store availability beginning October 23.

Apple recently announced that customers will be able to get ready for iPhone Duo pre-orders beginning October 12, and you can read more about that here.

title: Next-gen Google TV Streamer in the works with microphones, presence sensing, & new remote
snippet: 9to5Google can report that development on a next-generation Google TV Streamer is underway. more…
fullText:
9to5Google can report that development on a next-generation Google TV Streamer is underway. 

According to a source familiar with the matter, the new Google TV device retains the same general design. The width is narrower for a slightly more compact footprint. 

The big upgrade is the presence of microphones on the Google TV Streamer itself. There are cutouts on the slanted, pill-shaped surface that will listen for “Hey Google” commands. 

	

Another new hardware feature is presence sensing. Last year, TCL launched the first Google TV with that capability to turn on the Google Photos screensaver when someone enters the room. If you get close, the display shows ambient information like the time and weather.

	

Meanwhile, the new Google TV Streamer will be powered by a faster processor and offer more storage than the current model’s 32GB.

Google is also updating the included remote. The design is largely the same but with two more shortcuts joining the existing buttons for YouTube and Netflix. Additionally, the Find My Remote button remains on the back of the streaming device. 

We don’t have any information on when this next Google TV Streamer is launching. There was a four-year gap between the Chromecast with Google TV 4K and the Google TV Streamer, with the lower-end HD dongle coming in between the two. This refresh comes as Google raised the price of the existing unit by $50 in August.

title: Googlebook’s app situation is a mess, and not just because things are missing
snippet: Having been using a Googlebook for the better part of a week, there are any number of headaches I could talk about, but easily the biggest problem I’m running into thus far is the app situation. Frankly, it’s a mess. more…
fullText:
Having been using a Googlebook for the better part of a week, there are any number of headaches I could talk about, but easily the biggest problem I’m running into thus far is the app situation. Frankly, it’s a mess.

Googlebook, like Chromebook, was never going to be in a “good” place for apps. The Android-based platform sets up a more capable foundation for the future but, without a major push from Google and partners, it was always going to result in a rough start. 

And, yeah, it’s a rough start.

The “main” issue is around desktop-class apps and programs. Staples like the Adobe suite are simply not here, and there’s no easy way to replace them. Not to mention the depth of niche apps that have been built out in the Windows and macOS over the decades. At launch, Googlebook was never going to compete with that, though I’d argue that stripping away the Linux support ChromeOS did have isn’t exactly helping matters.

	

The problem I’m finding much more frustrating is around the apps Googlebook can access, and the messy situation around that.

The Google Play Store is your main way to obtain apps on Googlebook. Android apps are the preferred method and, in time, I’m sure that’ll work better than it does today. But, at the moment, Google’s stopgap to varying levels of quality for Android apps on desktop was to give five quality labels to any given app. 

Built for mobile: Hasn’t been tested for desktop

Better on the website: The web app/browser version has full features and/or better performance

Compatible with Desktop: Works with mouse/keyboard controls

Optimized for Desktop: “Adapted for a comfortable desktop experience”

Made for Desktop: “Built for desktop with specialized features and controls”

These are all applied by Google — developers have no direct control.

In my book, that’s wildly confusing for the end user, especially as the Play Store doesn’t link out to where you can use the web app for the Android apps it tries to steer you away from.

And it sadly should steer you away from some apps. 

Telegram is a great example of my frustration. The Android app is “better on the website,” and that’s incredibly true. The Android app is broken on Googlebook in a lot of ways, but the most frustrating is that the enter key doesn’t send a message. But, on the flip side, the web app isn’t that much better, as I’ve frequently run into cases where it misbehaves or even crashes. 

Slack continues to be a daily source of frustration, with the Android app being truly a terrible experience on anything other than a phone, and the web app unable to be installed. This is not some niche or trivial app, it’s something that millions rely on for daily work on their laptops. 

Spotify says that it is “Optimized for desktop” and, while it’s not bad, the phone UI doesn’t even scale as well here as it does on a foldable. It gets better when the “Now Playing” panel is expanded out, but it’s still not on par with other desktop platforms. “Optimized” just feels like the wrong word for this label. “Compatible” feels more apt for this particular example, but Google’s categories are way too specific to let that work.

“Optimized for desktop” according to who, exactly?

	

There’s no easy solution here.

Googlebook is in its early days and, while the foundation presents a better future, the “now” is a huge headache, and one I struggle to get on board with because, well why would you subject yourself to this? Good Windows laptops are easy to find. The MacBook Air is easy to find for $1,099 (cheaper than most Googlebooks!). Good, established platforms that simply don’t have these shortcomings. Why would I give that up for some Android integrations that don’t even work with my phone yet?

Sound off in the comments, I’d love to hear what you think about this problem and how it impacts your view of Googlebook.

title: OLED MacBook Pro to help boost premium display shipments, per report
snippet: A new Counterpoint Research report says Apple’s next-generation MacBook Pro will help drive a 50% increase in OLED notebook display shipments in 2026 alone. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new Counterpoint Research report says Apple’s next-generation MacBook Pro will help drive a 50% increase in OLED notebook display shipments in 2026 alone. Here are the details.

New MacBook Pro and premium AI PCs expected to fuel demand

In a report released today, Counterpoint Research projects that advanced notebook display shipments will grow 11% in 2026 compared to 2025, with OLED notebook display shipments expected to rise 50% for the period.

The report notes that the 11% growth in advanced notebook display shipments will comfortably outperform the broader notebook display market, which Counterpoint says it expects to decline 3% year over year.

Counterpoint says it also expects OLED to widen its lead over MiniLED in the advanced notebook display market, rising from 56% of shipments in 2025 to 75% in 2026, while MiniLED is expected to drop from 44% to 25%.

The research company says part of the growth in OLED notebook panel shipments is expected to come from Apple’s adoption of the technology in its next-generation MacBook Pro, currently rumored to be announced on October 27 with a touchscreen display and a redesigned, significantly lighter chassis.

Here’s Counterpoint:

OLED notebook display shipments are forecast to rise 50% in 2026 and another 24% in 2027. Apple’s anticipated adoption of OLED in next-generation MacBook Pro models, alongside continued demand for premium AI PCs, is expected to drive this growth.

Another factor contributing to OLED’s growth, Counterpoint says, is technology and manufacturing advances such as tandem OLED architectures, which improve brightness, power efficiency, and panel longevity.

Apple already uses tandem OLED in the iPad Pro, where two OLED layers work together to deliver higher full-screen brightness. The company is widely expected to use a similar two-stack tandem OLED architecture for the upcoming 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects OLED notebook panel shipments to grow at a compounded annual rate of 26% between 2024 and 2030, while panel revenue is forecast to grow at 35% per year over the same period.

title: Researchers uncover new DarkSword spyware variant affecting unpatched iPhones
snippet: iVerify released a report today detailing P7 DarkSword, a new variant of the malware associated with the DarkSword iPhone exploit chain uncovered earlier this year. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
iVerify released a report today detailing P7 DarkSword, a new variant of the malware associated with the DarkSword iPhone exploit chain uncovered earlier this year. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Earlier this year, Google and iVerify revealed two sophisticated iPhone hacking tools known as Coruna and DarkSword, both of which chained multiple iOS vulnerabilities to compromise devices running outdated system versions.

In DarkSword’s case, once an iPhone was compromised, attackers could deploy additional malware with access to sensitive data.

Coruna targeted devices running iOS 13 through iOS 17.2.1, while DarkSword affected iPhones running iOS 18.4 through iOS 18.7.

This led Apple to release system updates for the affected older iOS versions, including iOS 15.8.7, iOS 16.7.15, and iOS 18.7.7. Apple went as far as to take the unusual step of making iOS 18.7.7 available to devices that could install iOS 26, so users who elected not to update to the latest system version would also remain protected against DarkSword.

At the time, Google said DarkSword was being used by multiple commercial surveillance vendors and suspected state-sponsored actors, with attacks observed against targets in Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Malaysia, and Ukraine.

New DarkSword variant found in the wild

Today, iVerify announced the discovery of P7 DarkSword, a previously unseen variant it found while investigating an infection on the iPhone of an employee at a financial institution just two months ago.

In additional details shared with 9to5Mac, iVerify noted that the P7 expands compatibility to iOS 18.7, up from iOS 18.6 in the earlier variant it had been tracking. Other DarkSword deployments observed by Google had already supported iOS 18.7.

The company also said the threat actor behind P7 is distributing it through malicious ads as part of watering-hole attacks, meaning victims do not necessarily appear to be individually targeted. Instead, users can be caught in broader campaigns simply by encountering malicious or compromised web content.

From the report:

In August 2026 we investigated a DarkSword infection that turned out to be a previously unseen variant, which we call P7 DarkSword. The name P7 comes from the threat actor’s use of the p7_ variable prefix in modifications to original DarkSword’s code. Compared with the variants we usually observe, P7 reduces its on-device footprint, adds on-device keychain and crypto-wallet theft, and adds two way C2 communication with the attacker’s infrastructure. This post describes the investigation, the variant’s capabilities, and the indicators that can be used to detect it._

The report says that P7 DarkSword improves on earlier variants in three main areas: stealth, stability, and functionality. The new variant reduces logging and the number of process injections it performs, uses browser storage to avoid repeatedly exploiting the same device, and expands its data-stealing capabilities.

iVerify also told 9to5Mac that the changes appear to reflect substantial work by the operators rather than simple AI-assisted modifications. The company says P7 is much better at hiding itself and cleaning up its behavior, so previous indicators of compromise (IOCs) are no longer valid.

Most notably, iVerify says P7 can extract Keychain data directly on the iPhone before sending it to the attackers, instead of copying the entire Keychain database for processing elsewhere.

P7 DarkSword can also target crypto-wallet data, and introduces more advanced two-way communication with the attackers’ command-and-control infrastructure.

That two-way communication also gives attackers considerably more control over an infected device. According to iVerify, P7 can receive commands to retrieve arbitrary files, upload photos, inventory installed apps, access Apple Notes databases, collect data from individual app containers, and scan the device’s filesystem.

By default, the spyware checks in with the attackers’ command-and-control server every 15 seconds for new instructions, although that interval can be changed remotely.

It’s worth noting that P7 is not a new iOS vulnerability, but rather a new version of the malware deployed after a successful DarkSword compromise. iVerify does not say which iOS version was running on the device where P7 was discovered in August.

fullText:

According to a few users on Reddit, Google Home isn’t properly adjusting color on smart bulbs. Users say it hasn’t been limited to just one brand, but devices across multiple brands like Philips Hue, Tuya, and Lumiman. The issue was affecting both voice controls and app controls, which are usually more reliable and easier to adjust. But the color sliders did nothing for affected users.

Google responded to the Reddit thread to say a fix is currently rolling out. The post author has since updated the thread to say their voice commands and app are now reliably controlling bulb color.

The post was barely a day old when Google first let users know it was working on a fix. Just a few hours later, an update was rolling out. The quick turnaround is likely appreciated for this bug because it broke a critical component and selling point for not only Google Home but also smart bulb manufacturers.

	

Color control might have been broken while Google works on other additions to the app. Monthly updates are being released to address the functions and bugs appearing as Google Assistant fades into the background, which has officially happened as of last month.

Were/are you experiencing a bug that broke smart bulb color control? It should be fixed now, but if it isn’t, let us know.

title: Apple has reportedly increased its iPhone Duo orders by 30%

fullText:
A new report by Securities Times in China indicates Apple is now anticipating much higher demand for iPhone Duo than initially expected, despite pre-orders not starting until later this week.

Initial iPhone Duo supply for 2026 reportedly nearing 10 million units

Apple launches iPhone Duo pre-orders this Friday, October 16. And you’ll be able to start your pre-order process for the fastest checkout later today.
