title: Amazon’s new Alexa Tablets are an iPad-inspired reboot, complete with the Play Store
snippet: Amazon has an all-new lineup of tablets ready to tempt you this holiday season, and for once, you might actually want to buy them. While the company has tried in previous years to make an upmarket play for relevancy in the tablet space, these new Alexa Tablets — RIP “Fire” — have the one thing everyone’s wanted for years: actual Play Store support. more…
fullText:
Amazon has an all-new lineup of tablets ready to tempt you this holiday season, and for once, you might actually want to buy them. While the company has tried in previous years to make an upmarket play for relevancy in the tablet space, these new Alexa Tablets — RIP “Fire” — have the one thing everyone’s wanted for years: actual Play Store support.

Yes, a decade after ditching the “Kindle” branding in its tablet lineup, Amazon is ditching the Fire brand entirely for its new lineup of iPad competitors. That’s not me trying to write off its Android-powered rivals; rather, the sizes and designs all make for devices that, frankly, look like iPad knock-offs. Alexa Tablets come in three sizes: an 8-inch entry-level iPad Mini competitor, an 11-inch base iPad-esque slate, and a 12-inch “Pro” model that looks to be the most unique of the bunch. They’re all designed with aluminum bodies and, despite being much more expensive than the Fire tablets they’re replacing, still manage to undercut most of the market.

The 8.7-inch 60Hz Alexa Tablet 8 features 4GB of RAM, up to 128GB of storage, and comes in graphite, rosette, and teal, while the 90Hz 11-inch Alexa Tablet 11 features 8GB of RAM, up to 128GB of storage, and adds matcha and amethyst to the mix. Both run on a MediaTek 8189 8-core processor, a relatively recent chipset that appeared in a handful of seemingly-unreleased ChromeOS devices over the past year or so, before landing in these budget tablets. While I wouldn’t say there’s much to write home here about the specs — and again, the design is just absolutely a blatant copy of the iPad — it certainly sounds like a big upgrade over their predecessors.

	

And really, that comes down to the software. Despite Amazon’s current Android-less strategy on its Fire TV devices, the company seems to be doubling down on Android with its tablets. While it does have a unique launcher designed to push Alexa+, these things run proper Android, complete with the Play Store front and center on the device. YouTube is one of the highlighted apps on their store listings, and as someone who maintained Play Store sideloading guides at two different tech websites over the past decade, I can certainly say I never saw it coming. I have no idea how the actual software experience will feel day-to-day, but in terms of app support, it’s one problem that’s finally solved.

	

The star of the show, of course, is the 12-inch Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. This is, bar none, the most premium tablet Amazon has ever shipped, with a price that matches. It combines a 2.8K 3:2 120Hz display with quad speakers, 8GB of RAM, 128GB of storage, and a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 processor. That’s a real processor, and while I wouldn’t say it’s worthy of being called a flagship chipset, it’s undoubtedly the most powerful chip Amazon’s ever used. It’s a good sign when you’re using the same processor that a budget gaming-focused brand like Poco used just a year or two ago.

The 12-inch model also comes in an optional “nanomatte” version for an anti-glare experience, which also allows you to upgrade your RAM and storage to 16GB and 256GB, respectively. 16GB of RAM in an Amazon tablet — it’s a new day after all. And like its last attempt to go full-premium, the company does offer optional stylus and keyboard accessories for road warriors on a budget.

The Alexa Tablet 8 starts at $230 for the base 64GB model with lockscreen ads, or $250 without, while the Alexa Tablet 11 starts at $330 for its base model, or $350 for the ad-free version. Both feature a 128GB upgrade for $50 more. The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro starts at $500 for the base 128GB model; the nanomatte upgrade will run you $50 more. Meanwhile, that high-end 16/256 variant costs a whopping $680, and while that might sound pretty expensive on paper, it comes in well under Samsung’s latest 12-inch tablet for anyone who doesn’t need that level of processing power. Oh, and absolutely no ads on any of the 12 Pro models — the price you see is the price you pay, no upgrades necessary.

title: Android Auto rolling out fix that stops auto-playing music when you start your car
snippet: Google has confirmed that a fix is rolling out for a bug that leaves Android Auto briefly auto-playing music when your car starts, even if you have autoplay disabled. more…
fullText:
Google has confirmed that a fix is rolling out for a bug that leaves Android Auto briefly auto-playing music when your car starts, even if you have autoplay disabled.

Most of the time you’d want Android Auto to start playing music as soon as it starts up. That’s one of the big benefits of the platform, after all. But if you don’t want music to start playing automatically, there’s a toggle that lets you disable autoplay.

It just hasn’t been working properly for a while.

For some, Android Auto would start playing music briefly when your vehicle starts before ending playback a few seconds later. It’s more than a bit frustrating, but a fix is apparently rolling out.

	

In a post on Reddit, Google confirmed that “unsolicited play commands” will no longer be sent during startup if autoplay is turned off in Android Auto. This is alongside other improvements to autoplay including a prompt to opt out of autoplay if Android Auto notices you frequently pause playback immediately after it starts.

We’ve made a couple of bug fixes so autoplay* works more predictably and accurately based on your listening preferences:

Autoplay app selection: Apps that you haven’t recently or ever used will no longer be selected for autoplay.

One-tap opt-out: If you prefer manual playback and frequently pause autoplay, Android Auto will notice and provide a convenient one-tap notification to quickly disable autoplay.

Infotainment startup handling: We’re rolling out a fix so unsolicited play commands won’t be sent when you have autoplay turned off.

There’s no mention of which Android Auto update fixes autoplay, but it is “rolling out,” Google says.

title: HomeView and More: Everything Apple Announced at Its ‘Welcome Home’ Event
snippet: Apple is making a sweeping new entry into home tech.
fullText:
Apple wants to have a much bigger presence in your house. On Tuesday, the maker of Macs and iPhones unveiled a sweeping lineup of new products presenting a range of options for home management, security and entertainment.

The centerpiece is the Apple HomeView smart display, which can sit on a tabletop or be mounted on a wall. In its tabletop version, with its domed base, it echoes the iconic iMac G4 from the early 2000s. 

But this is a device for a new era, brimming with Siri AI and personalization features and built for household interactions.

			

More from CNET

“Apple HomeView is designed to be shared by everyone in the home yet feel completely personal to each user,” Greg Joswiak, Apple’s senior vice president of worldwide marketing, said in a statement. 

The products altogether represent a big new smart home push for Apple, which for years has largely left that field to be dominated by Amazon and Google. One thing that could work in Apple’s favor, said Ben Wood, chief analyst at FDM CCS Insight, is its reputation for making technology easier to use than the alternatives. 

“In typical Apple fashion, setting up the new products is simple: you just hold your iPhone near the device and add it as easily as pairing new Apple headphones or Watch,” Wood told CNET via email. “That’s quite a contrast to other smart home products where you have to download a specific app, scan QR codes and more.”

Tuesday’s “Welcome Home” event took place just over a month after Apple’s September introduction of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max and the folding iPhone Duo.

Here’s everything Apple just announced: 

The HomeView is designed as the hub for a range of capabilities, including making FaceTime calls, playing music and managing smart home devices. 

It features a 7-inch square Liquid Retina display and Apple’s A18 chip and can be controlled by by touch or voice. Apple sees its new Siri AI as central to the experience of using the HomeView.

It recognizes up to six users by their faces and can be set up with a personalized home screen for each. Like on the Apple Watch, display customization options allow for a wide range of screen designs. The Home Camera face can livestream up to nine video feeds simultaneously.

Just like an Apple Watch: You can customize the look of your HomeView, depending on your preference, from standard clocks to calendar to family to Snoopy.Apple

The HomeView works with the new Apple Home Collection devices – more on that below – as well as other Matter and Works with Apple Home accessories

The tabletop version is available in four colors: silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray

The wall mount version comes in either silver or space gray.

Preorders start Tuesday for people in the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and India, on Thursday for those in Singapore, and on Friday for those in South Africa, with availability in all those countries beginning Nov. 13. The HomeView is not available in EU countries because Siri AI not available in iOS there.

The HomeView is priced at $299 for both the tabletop and wall-mount versions. There are two dedicated wall mounts, at $60 and $80, that can be preordered starting Tuesday. A third wall mount available will be available in early 2027 for $130.

Apple Home Collection

The Home Collection line of products includes smart home cameras for both indoors and outdoors, thermostats, temperature sensors, a video doorbell and a smart lock designed in collaboration with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. In its press release, Apple described the gear as having a “clean, minimal aesthetic.”

The lineup includes four LG camera devices: 

The $250 Video Doorbell, with dual cameras (for views of visitors and packages), plus a spotlight and a chime that plays through the HomeView, HomePod and HomePod Mini.

The $400 Floodlight Cam, which features motion sensing and low-light color night vision.

The simpler $200 Outdoor Cam. 

The $200 Indoor Cam – for privacy: tilts up and down for you to monitor while you’re away, and down to stop monitoring when you’re at home.

Apple emphasized the privacy aspects of the devices. For instance, the Indoor Cam will tilt down when you’re at home. Camera footage, the company said, is processed locally or via Private Cloud Compute. For those with an iCloud Plus subscription, up to 10 days’ worth of video history can be stored in encrypted form.

The collection also includes the $350 LG Smart Deadbolt Lock, which recognizes when known users approach and can unlock automatically and which can work in conjunction with the video doorbell. 

Two thermostats are in the mix, one from LG and the other from Schneider. Each costs $200, and separate temperature sensors cost $40 apiece. 

Availability for the Home Collection products begins in December, with certain accessories available starting in early 2027.

The new Apple TV 4K can be paired with up to four HomePod speakers.Apple

Apple HomePod Mini 2

Apple is expanding its HomePod line with the new $149 HomePod Mini 2 smart speaker, or as Apple puts it, “conversational assistant.” It’s the first major upgrade to the HomePod lineup in years.

It can sync up with other HomePods or with Apple TV. For first time, the company said, users can create four-speaker surround sound with new Apple TV 4K. Buyers can choose from five colors: pink, green, blue, white and midnight.

“When paired with the new Apple TV 4K, it delivers our most immersive home theater setup yet,” Kaiann Drance, Apple’s vice president of worldwide home product marketing, said in a statement.

Preorders for the HomePod Mini 2 begin Tuesday for people in the US and about two dozen countries and regions, with availability starting Oct. 30. Siri AI access will arrive in a future software update.

Apple TV 4K

The new Apple TV 4K features Apple’s A19 chip for up to 50% faster CPU performance and up to 2x faster GPU performance, the company said. Besides streaming shows and movies, it can also serve as a home hub – for instance, doorbell notifications will appear on the screen.

It has three built-in far-field microphones so that you can talk to Siri AI. 

Preorders start Tuesday, with availability Nov. 13 for customers in the US and 29 other countries and regions. Pricing starts at $299 or $49.83 per month for six months.

CNET Principal Writer Katie Collins contributed to this article.

According to the report, Apple has named Steve Smith as its new mergers and acquisitions leader. Smith replaces Adrian Perica, who joined Apple in 2009 and led the M&A and corporate development teams for over a decade. Bloomberg describes Smith as Perica’s “longtime lieutenant.” He will report to CFO Kevan Parekh.

Perica, meanwhile, is taking on a “more prominent position” within Apple’s services division. He has led iCloud, Fitness+, and Apple News since 2023 and will now report directly to services boss Eddy Cue.

In fact, Perica, along with Apple Music leader Oliver Schusser, is seen as a potential successor to Cue:

Though Perica is relinquishing responsibility for M&A, the move gives him a more prominent position within Cue’s organization at a time when the services chief is assessing multiple potential successors. Many Apple employees familiar with the situation believe Perica and Oliver Schusser, the executive overseeing Apple Music, are the leading candidates to eventually replace Cue. Another possibility under discussion is splitting Cue’s responsibilities between the two executives.

Additionally, today’s Bloomberg says that Apple is promoting Carson Oliver to vice president of the App Store, reporting to Cue. Apple Fellow Phil Schiller led the App Store until he stepped down in August.

Apple officially confirmed that it will hold a product launch event tomorrow, October 13. With a “Welcome home” tagline, the launch is expected to focus on new smart home products. Here’s everything to expect at tomorrow’s Apple event.

Apple ‘Welcome home’ details

There are two components to the event, as Ryan outlined. There is the in-person experience for members of the press in New York City, as well as what Mark Gurman has called an “online video presentation.”

This suggests we can expect press releases and a video (or videos) to drop around 9 a.m. ET/6 a.m. PT on October 13. Apple hasn’t confirmed this, so the actual launch might vary. At a minimum, though, we know it will announce something on October 13, and some people will see it in person while the rest of us follow along from home.

What to expect

‘HomeView’ smart display

Tomorrow’s headlining announcement will be Apple’s long-rumored smart display product, which Bloomberg says will be called HomeView. Apple believes that this product can serve as a central hub for your house, powered by Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

According to Bloomberg, the device will have a 6-inch square display atop a half-dome base, with a metal arm holding it up. The HomeView will reportedly come in two variations: one that can be mounted on a wall and one that can sit on a countertop. Reports have likened the design to Apple’s iconic iMac G4.

One of the flagship features of the HomeView will be its ability to recognize multiple people in a household. Mark Gurman reports that it can recognize who is talking to it or approaching it and dynamically adjust what’s shown on the screen.

In terms of software, the HomeView reportedly mixes different elements of the Apple Watch, Apple TV, and iPad. This includes iPad-like app designs and Apple Watch-style icons. It will also heavily borrow from the iPhone for widgets and StandBy mode.

Finally, while HomeView will be announced tomorrow, the latest reporting is that it won’t be available until sometime in November. 

New Apple TV 4K

Apple is also expected to announce a new Apple TV 4K, its first update to the set-top box since November 2022. The new Apple TV will look the same as its predecessor, but it will reportedly include the A19 or A19 Pro chip.

That upgraded chip will allow Apple to bring Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features to the Apple TV for the first time.

The new Apple TV could also have built-in microphones for Siri interactions. The Siri Remote, meanwhile, might add a speaker to make it easier to find if you misplace it. 

Apple is also reportedly working on new software features for the Apple TV and HomePod. For example, there are code references to a new feature that would let you arrange four full-sized HomePods in a surround sound system when paired with Apple TV.

HomePod mini 2

The HomePod mini will also get its first proper upgrade tomorrow. The big change here will be a new S10 chip that is much faster than the current model’s S5 processor, bringing support for Siri AI. For context, the S5 chip used in the current HomePod mini is the same chip Apple debuted with the Apple Watch Series 5.

Beyond the faster chip, the new HomePod mini 2 will reportedly come in new colors:

Pink

White

Green

Blue

Black

Bonus: New ‘second-party’ smart home gear

Finally, Apple is working with LG on new “second-party” accessories for HomeKit. Apple reportedly collaborated with LG to co-develop products including a smart lock, thermostat, doorbell, and multiple cameras.

Bloomberg says Apple won’t release these accessories for “at least a few more months.” They could still be shown off as part of Apple’s broader home strategy tomorrow, though.

Apple’s new ‘second-party’ accessories for Home are bigger than we thought, per leak

Leaked images reveal Apple’s new Home smart lock, thermostat, more for LG

Apple’s new Home cameras and doorbell with LG revealed in leaked images

Apple’s new ‘second-party’ HomeKit products will have this exclusive iPhone feature

Wrap up

While we obviously have a pretty good idea of what Apple will announce tomorrow thanks to these rumors, I’m still really excited to see the company unveil its home roadmap. It’s felt like a category Apple has neglected for far too long, and one it might finally start taking seriously tomorrow.

What are you most excited to see at Apple’s “Welcome home” event tomorrow? Are you planning to buy the all-new HomeView or upgrade your Apple TV and HomePod mini? Let us know down in the comments.

snippet: Apple TV today announced “Heart,” an original eight-episode true-crime podcast involving two men linked by a donated heart and the same terrible demise. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple TV today announced “Heart,” an original eight-episode true-crime podcast involving two men linked by a donated heart and the same terrible demise. Here are the details.

The lives and deaths of two men linked by a single heart

Although far fewer in number than its movies and series, Apple TV has steadily expanded its lineup of original podcasts since 2021, releasing several titles spanning true crime, investigative journalism, comedy, and companion podcasts for its shows.

That includes “Adrift,” “Unicorn Girl,” “Pluribus: The Official Podcast,” and “Magnificent Jerk.”

Today, the platform announced “Heart,” an eight-episode true-crime original podcast hosted by Karen Kilgariff, set to premiere on October 19.

Here’s Apple TV on what to expect from “Heart”:

When Sonny Graham receives a lifesaving heart transplant, he falls in love with his donor’s widow. What local newspapers hail as a miraculous love story takes a tragic turn when Sonny dies — the same way as his heart donor, Terry Cottle. In both cases, the official conclusion is suicide. As friends and family recall changes in Sonny’s behavior after the transplant, some question whether the heart he received could have carried traces of the donor’s trauma.

Apple TV says “Heart” is the result of years of investigative reporting, with the team behind the podcast piecing together court documents, public records, and firsthand accounts to investigate the circumstances surrounding both men’s deaths and their impact on their families.

Apple TV subscribers will get access to all eight episodes of “Heart” on October 19, while nonsubscribers will get the first three episodes on that date, followed by weekly releases every Monday through November 23.

Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month or as part of the Apple One bundle. It features hit TV shows and movies like Ted Lasso, Severance, The Studio, The Morning Show, Shrinking, and Silo.

Apple has confirmed a special ‘Welcome home’ product launch event is happening next Tuesday, October 13. But it hasn’t yet said whether there will be a keynote video. Here’s what we know.

Apple hasn’t confirmed ‘Welcome home’ keynote, but Mark Gurman says an ‘online video presentation’ is coming

Like its smart home event on Oct. 13, the next launch will include an online video presentation and in-person component for the press

Press are attending a NYC “Apple Experience” that starts at 9:00 a.m. ET. So if there is an announcement video, we’ll likely see it debut online then—much earlier than the typical keynote time.

title: Apple Home Event Rumor Roundup: Everything We Expect to See Tomorrow
snippet: Reports say Apple will be announcing a new home display with Siri AI — and possibly much, much more.
fullText:
Coming only a few short weeks after Apple’s big fall event where the company announced its first foldable iPhone Duo, Apple is holding another event tomorrow called “Welcome Home.” Instead of focusing on iPhones and Macs, this event will be announcing Apple’s home tech, including what we expect to be all-new devices and new ways to use Siri AI.

CNET will be at the event to give you live updates and get hands-on with Apple’s plans for your home, but for now here’s what the rumors tell us. If reports are right, Apple may be releasing a new kind of smart display, an update to the HomePod line, an Apple TV and more. Let’s take a look.

A Siri smart display, possibly the “HomeView”

An Apple smart display could allow Siri to get much more creative.Bloomberg/Getty Images

For more than a year, Apple has been rumored to be readying a Siri-focused smart display hub for the home. Now we have specific reports from Mark Gurman at Bloomberg that say Apple’s event will focus on the display, which is possibly called the HomeView and will ship sometime in November. This device is ruored to have an A18 chip and come in two designs, one for tables and one for wall mounting.

			

More from CNET

Smart displays can add a lot of functionality to smart speakers, if you don’t mind using voice assistants.  Smart touchscreens are great for getting visual information, watching videos or viewing to-do lists, so a display like this is likely to have a bit of Apple TV and Safari in it, too. While the Apple TV 4K, iPad and current HomePod models can already act as HomeKit hubs, I expect Apple to offer a real UI and UX experience designed for smart displays, making it a stronger argument for having in your home alongside other devices.

However, a Siri smart display faces steep competition against established brands like Amazon’s Echo Shows and Google’s Nest Hubs, so Apple will need to carefully differentiate this “HomeView.”

Is it likely? I think it’s very likely, based on how many insider reports have mentioned this smart display, but I don’t think we have a good idea exactly how it will look and operate yet. Watch for more news on this tomorrow.

Updates to the HomePod line

Is a new HomePod Mini on the way?Chris Monroe/CNET

Along with a smart display, rumors are flying that Apple will give its HomePod smart speaker line the first major update in years. It’s the ideal time to update the HomePod line, too, although it’s possible some of these reports have confused plans for a smart display with a new smart speaker, both of which could fall under the HomePod label.

If a new HomePod speaker is on the horizon, reports indicate that it would be a new type of HomePod Mini. That’s not surprising — the original HomePod has often been critiqued for being over $300, which is why Apple focused on the less expensive Mini model afterward. One welcome leak I’ve seen is that there will be new colors for the HomePod Mini 2, including green and pink, and a faster S-series chip.

Is it likely? Yes, I’d say this is about as likely as a Siri smart display, if Apple wants to continue developing the HomePod line. Hopefully we’ll be able to hear how it sounds in person if Apple is ready to unleash a new smart speaker. 

A new Apple TV

Apple TV is due for an upgrade, too.Geoffrey Morrison/CNET

The same reports that say a smart display and new HomePod are on the way also mention Apple is planning to release a new Apple TV model. This model is rumored to have upgraded specs, with a faster N1 processor, 8GB RAM, Wi-Fi 7 and an upgraded Siri remote, possibly with more AI features.

It’s a product line that’s sort of connected to the smart home, especially if Apple is launching a smart display. The company hasn’t released a new set-top box since 2022, so it’s about time for another. This could also give the Apple TV new hardware for extra Siri AI tricks. There’s also been some speculation that this will be compatible with the new HomePods, allowing you to set up multiple units in a surround sound-style home cinema. 

Is it likely? I think it’s strange that Apple would combine smart home products with a TV announcement, as they’re not especially related. But the reports we have about a new Apple TV are very specific, so it looks like there’s a strong chance Apple will update the line, although we don’t know if we’ll be able to get hands-on with new models.

Little Apple security cams — with no recording

Recent rumors says Apple is ready to enter the home security world with its own products. Although we don’t know much, reports from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman say these will be tiny cameras that, interestingly, won’t record any video. No recording means Apple won’t have to worry about cloud storage and may be able to avoid charging extra subscriptions for them.

The cameras are rumored to have some kind of presence-sensing or human-recognizing technology as well as AI video descriptions, suggesting Apple Home will be running analysis on the video even if it won’t record permanently. The phrase “facial recognition” was also mentioned, but this doesn’t seem nearly as likely to me. This may be related to a rumor about Apple’s Ring-like doorbell camera, which may come with Face ID for unlocking a door, but this would likely be separate from the non-recording indoor security cameras.

Is it likely? I’m betting on some kind of home security announcement, and I expect Apple would like to have its own camera line, but I don’t know if this exact product will be released. However, the extra details do lend this rumor legitimacy.

An LG collab for a new thermostat

Apple may be partnering with LG for some smart home devices, and there are even reportedly leaked product concept photos circulating on the internet. One of the biggest potential releases is an Apple-friendly thermostat. The photos show a round, Nest-like thermostat dial, and rumors say it will include far-sight presence sensing, a humidity sensor and several temperature calibration options.

2. LG Smart Thermostat

•  Settings for Far Sight Display, Humidity Display, Brightness, Language.

•  Calibrated Temperature/Temperature Offset options. pic.twitter.com/Q8AAaxy4ey

— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 7, 2026

Alongside the thermostat, the Apple/LG combo is expected to release a sensor that can measure the temperature at specific locations and feed that information back to the thermostat hub. That would be no surprise, because models from Nest, Ecobee and others have similar satellite sensors, although Apple’s may have adhesive strips to attach its version to the wall.

Apple partnered with LG years ago to support Apple-friendly security cameras, but those lines were rarely updated and quickly became obsolete. Maybe Apple is ready to try again with a different approach.

Is it likely? If Apple really is partnering with LG for a new wave of home devices, I think a thermostat is likely. But this is starting to be a lot of products to announce at a single October event that won’t be publicly streamed. 

Further LG collabs for smart lock and maybe more 

The other big rumor centering around an LG collaboration is an Apple smart lock. While many smart locks work with Apple and Apple Home Keys, the tech giant hasn’t been involved in the development of a smart lock before. 

It could have automatic unlocking, tapping your phone to unlock and a variety of keypad management options. That’s not surprising, but the rumored product images show a round, twist-to-unlock, light-up outdoor keypad, and I haven’t seen anything like that before.

If Apple does release a smart lock, Ring will have beaten it to the punch with its own announcement of its first-ever lock, which will include Alexa compatibility and a unique thumbturn that can generate a charge when the battery dies.

EXCLUSIVE 👀

First look at LG’s upcoming smart home lineup:

LG Video Doorbell Wired

LG Floodlight Cam

LG Outdoor Cam Plug-In

LG Indoor Cam Plug-In pic.twitter.com/vblGECQLM1

— そすのふか (@ringo_tech) October 7, 2026

Other rumors and purported product images suggest the LG partnership could also yield a video doorbell, floodlight camera, outdoor camera and indoor camera. These seem to be LG-branded devices, however, and I can’t imagine Apple releasing products that look like this. 

Is it likely? Now this is a lot of new gadgets to announce at once. I think a smart lock is about as likely as a smart thermostat; those are both strong fields for Apple to enter. For the rest of the cameras, I’m doubtful. The indoor camera could be connected to the rumors of Apple’s no-video model. If the LG partnership line is this large, I wouldn’t be surprised if Apple is saving it for a separate announcement later on.

What role will Apple Intelligence play in all this?

Apple Intelligence will fuel many Siri AI capabilities in the Apple Home app. That’s especially true of AI video descriptions, which Apple is bringing to supported security cameras (there are very few right now, but some of Aqara’s camera hubs are compatible). I’m testing these uses of Apple Intelligence now, but if Apple releases any of its own security cameras, you can bet they’ll use AI features in the same way.

Will there be any iPad news at this event?

There are rumors that Apple will announce an iPad Mini sometime this month, but it probably doesn’t have much to do with this event. This is a strictly smart home-focused release.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Tyler Lacoma
						

						

							Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home						
					

											

								

											Tyler has worked on, lived with and tested all types of smart home and security technology for over a dozen years, explaining the latest features, privacy tricks and top recommendations.
With degrees in business management, literature and technical writing, Tyler takes every opportunity to play with the latest AI technology, push smart devices to their limits and occasionally throw cameras off his roof, all to find the best devices to trust in your life. He always checks with the renters (and pets) in his life to see what smart products can work for everyone, in every living situation. 
Living in beautiful Bend, Oregon, gives Tyler plenty of opportunities to test the latest tech in every kind of weather and temperature. But when not at work, he can be found hiking the trails, trying out a new food recipe for his loved ones, keeping up on his favorite reading or gaming with good friends.
